About the role
We are looking for an organised, accurate and service-driven Human Resource Administrator to support the day-to-day HR administration requirements of the business.
This role is responsible for ensuring that employee documentation, contracts, payroll inputs, benefits administration, onboarding and offboarding processes are completed accurately and within the required timelines. You will also act as a first point of contact for general HR administration queries and support the HR team with labour relations, compliance and reporting requirements.
The ideal candidate is someone who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment, takes pride in getting the detail right and understands the importance of confidentiality, responsive service and meeting deadlines.
What you’ll be responsible for
HR administration and employee support
• Act as the first point of contact for general HR administration queries.
• Provide employees and managers with accurate information and responsive support.
• Prepare and issue employment contracts, promotion letters, increase letters, incentive letters and other employee documentation.
• Maintain complete and accurate employee files and HR records.
• Ensure all employee documentation is properly authorised, signed and filed.
• Maintain confidentiality when working with employee and company information.
Onboarding and offboarding
• Coordinate the administration of new starters and ensure onboarding packs are ready before their first day.
• Ensure all starter documentation and approvals are received and processed.
• Support the enrolment of employees onto compulsory company benefits.
• Coordinate employee exits, including termination documentation, service certificates, UIF documents and system access termination.
• Submit offboarding requests and ensure access is removed within the required timelines.
Payroll administration
• Prepare and submit accurate monthly payroll inputs before the relevant payroll cut-off dates.
• Process information relating to new starters, terminations, employee changes, casual hours, allowances and attendance.
• Reconcile attendance registers and resolve discrepancies.
• Verify fixed-term contract renewals and employee allowances.
• Assist with the accurate processing of training bonds, notice pay and other approved deductions.
• Respond to payroll queries and work closely with the Payroll team to resolve any discrepancies.
Employee benefits
• Assist employees with medical aid, provident fund and other benefits-related queries.
• Enrol new employees onto compulsory benefits.
• Process Workers’ Compensation documentation within statutory timelines.
• Prepare and distribute UIF documentation and certificates of service.
• Process approved employee benefit and expense claims.
• Keep up to date with company benefits and communicate relevant changes to employees.
Training and reporting
• Maintain accurate induction and new-starter training records.
• Ensure new employees are scheduled for induction within the required timeframe.
• Monitor the completion of assigned LMS training.
• Prepare monthly induction and HR administration reports.
• Maintain relevant HR trackers and provide regular updates to the Senior HR Officer.
Labour relations and compliance
• Assist with the administration of disciplinary, grievance and CCMA matters.
• Prepare case files and supporting documentation for hearings.
• Maintain an updated tracker of active employee relations matters.
• Support the submission of documentation within statutory deadlines.
• Assist with HR compliance reviews and OHASA documentation.
• Distribute updated policies and ensure signed acknowledgements are received and filed.
• Support internal and external HR audits.
What we’re looking for
• Matric is essential.
• A relevant HR qualification would be advantageous.
• 2 to 3 years’ experience in an HR administration or HR support role.
• Working knowledge of basic South African labour legislation and HR practices.
• Experience with contracts, payroll inputs, employee records, benefits and onboarding administration.
• Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office or Google Workspace.
• Experience working with an HR information or payroll system would be advantageous.
Key competencies
• Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
• Excellent organisational and time-management skills.
• A responsive and customer-focused approach.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills.
• Professionalism and the ability to handle confidential information.
• The ability to manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
• Strong problem-solving skills and the confidence to escalate risks when necessary.
• The ability to work independently while contributing positively to the wider HR team.
• A sound understanding of HR administration processes and labour legislation.
What success will look like
Success in this role will be measured by the accuracy and completeness of HR documentation, the timely submission of payroll and statutory information, responsive employee support, smooth onboarding and offboarding processes, and consistent compliance with company policies and legal requirements. The role requires someone who can meet deadlines, minimise errors and resolve routine HR queries efficiently.

About iStore
iStore is the home of everything Apple and Africa’s largest Apple Premium Reseller. With more than 41 physical and online stores across Africa, we provide expert advice, Apple Authorised Repairs, Business and Education solutions, training, and technical support for everything Apple.
About the Role
We are looking for an experienced Credit Analyst to support the assessment and approval of customer finance applications across the iStore retail network.
This role is responsible for reviewing customer credit applications, assessing affordability and financial risk, and making sound credit decisions within agreed turnaround times. As our stores trade seven days a week, the successful candidate must be available to work retail hours, including weekends and public holidays.
The role requires someone who is analytical, decisive and customer-focused, while ensuring that all applications are assessed responsibly and in line with our credit policies and risk appetite.
Key Responsibilities
Credit Assessment and Decision-Making
• Review and analyse customer finance applications to determine creditworthiness and affordability.
• Make independent credit decisions within the required approval limits and service-level timeframes.
• Interpret credit bureau reports, customer financial information and supporting documentation.
• Identify potential credit, affordability, fraud and compliance risks.
• Approve, decline or refer applications in line with company credit policies and risk appetite.
• Clearly document the rationale for all credit decisions.
• Recommend appropriate risk-mitigation measures where required.
Customer and Portfolio Risk Management
• Monitor customer exposure, credit limits, risk ratings and account performance.
• Conduct regular credit reviews and ensure customer information remains accurate and up to date.
• Identify changes in customer risk profiles and escalate concerns where necessary.
• Support the responsible management of the consumer finance portfolio.
• Assist with the identification of trends, risks and potential areas of concern within the portfolio.
Retail and Business Support
• Provide efficient credit decision support to iStore teams across the retail network.
• Work closely with stores and internal stakeholders to resolve application queries and outstanding information.
• Balance responsible credit decision-making with the need to provide a positive customer experience.
• Communicate credit decisions clearly and professionally.
• Provide objective guidance on the risks, benefits and potential implications of applications.
• Support credit-related projects, reporting, data analysis and forecasting where required.
Qualifications and Experience
• Bachelor’s degree or relevant qualification in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Risk Management or a related field.
• Three to five years’ experience in credit analysis, consumer finance, retail finance, banking or a related environment.
• Experience assessing individual consumer credit applications.
• Strong understanding of the full credit lifecycle.
• Experience reading and interpreting credit bureau records.
• Sound knowledge of affordability assessments, financial analysis and credit risk principles.
• Experience working within credit policies, approval limits and service-level requirements.
• Proficiency in data analysis, reporting and Microsoft Excel.
• Experience in a high-volume retail or consumer finance environment would be advantageous.Working hours
This role supports a retail environment and requires flexibility to work:
• Weekends (Rotation, so not every weekend)
• Public holidays where required
• Retail trading hours
• Shifts or scheduled standby periods, where required
What we offer
• The opportunity to join a diverse team of passionate individuals.
• Exposure to one of the world’s leading technology brands.
• A fast-paced and challenging retail environment.
• The opportunity to expand your credit, risk and consumer finance experience.
• A role where your decisions directly support both the customer experience and the responsible growth of the business.
Competencies
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Sound judgement and the ability to make confident, objective decisions.
• High attention to detail and accuracy.
• Strong understanding of responsible lending and affordability principles.
• Ability to interpret complex credit and financial information.
• Good verbal and written communication skills.
• Strong time-management and organisational skills.
• Able to work effectively under pressure and manage high application volumes.
• Ethical, transparent and consistent in decision-making.
• Adaptable and comfortable working in a fast-paced retail environment.
• Strong relationship-building and stakeholder-management skills.
Background Checks
Should your application be successful, relevant background checks will be conducted. It will include criminal record, credit, identity, qualification and reference checks.

Role Purpose
Own and grow the commercial performance of the insurance portfolio, funeral and accident products, by understanding the customer, building trust, and turning insight into marketing decisions that grow quotes, policy sales, persistency and customer value.
This is a product marketing role, not a campaign coordination role, and not a Head of Marketing role. The Marketing Manager spends their time on the questions that move the numbers, why conversions are changing, where customers drop off or fail to take up, which journeys need fixing, which campaigns to prioritise, what customers are telling us, and how to grow customer value, and turns the answers into recommendations for leadership.
They spend very little time chasing artwork, loading campaigns, building project plans, scheduling emails or coordinating approvals. That work belongs to the Marketing Campaign Specialist.
Where the Role Sits
This role sits within the Growth & Engagement division and reports to the Executive: Growth & Engagement.
The operating model deliberately separates commercial ownership from campaign execution. The Marketing Manager decides what needs to happen and why. The Marketing Campaign Specialist decides how it is delivered and when it launches. This role briefs, prioritises and guides execution. It does not run production.
Three Clear Owners
Executive: Growth & Engagement – Owns the Strategy
Growth strategy, commercial priorities and portfolio direction. Investment decisions, cross-product strategy and executive stakeholder management.
Marketing Manager (This Role) – Owns the Performance
Product marketing performance, customer insight and customer journeys. Campaign priorities, product positioning, commercial recommendations, marketing optimisation and stakeholder alignment.
Marketing Campaign Specialist – Owns the Delivery
Campaign execution and production, workflow and asset management, creative coordination, compliance approvals, scheduling and launches, and project management.
How the Role Spends Its Time
Approximately 30% of the role is focused on product marketing and commercial performance.
Approximately 25% of the role is focused on customer journey optimisation.
Approximately 15% of the role is focused on customer insight and research.
Approximately 15% of the role is focused on performance analysis and reporting.
Approximately 10% of the role is focused on stakeholder management.
Approximately 5% of the role is focused on executive presentations and planning.
Core Responsibilities
• Product Marketing OwnershipOwn the commercial marketing performance of the insurance portfolio. Be accountable for customer growth, conversion, engagement, retention, cross-sell and marketing effectiveness. Translate business objectives into clear marketing priorities.
• Customer Journey OptimisationOwn the ongoing optimisation of the end-to-end customer journey: acquisition, onboarding, abandoned journeys, lifecycle communications, retention, reactivation and cross-sell. Identify friction, quantify its impact, and recommend improvements. Work closely with CRM and the Campaign Specialist to implement enhancements.
• Customer InsightBuild a deeper understanding of the customer than anyone else in the business through surveys, customer interviews, complaints, behavioural analysis, call listening, competitor monitoring and market trends. Turn that insight into concrete marketing improvements.
• Performance AnalysisMonitor performance across campaigns, channels, customer behaviour, conversion, engagement and ROI. Present insight, root cause, recommendation and action.
Never simply present data. Every report ends with a decision or a recommendation.
• Campaign PrioritisationDevelop campaign briefs and priorities, and give the Campaign Specialist clear direction on objective, target audience, messaging, offer and desired outcome. Review campaign performance and continuously optimise. This role directs campaigns. It does not produce them.
• Stakeholder ManagementWork closely with Product, Credit, Risk, Analytics, CRM, Creative Studio, the Campaign Specialist, Compliance and Customer Service to ensure marketing activity supports broader commercial objectives.
Insurance Focus
Beyond the core, the Insurance Marketing Manager owns the commercial marketing of the funeral and accident portfolio specifically through:
• Quote generation and policy sales growth
• Building and protecting customer trust in the products
• NTU (not-taken-up) improvement, converting quotes and approvals into active policies
• Persistency, retention and premium growth
• Cross-sell of insurance from the lending base
• Clear, reassuring claims communications that reinforce trustPrimary KPIs
Success in the role is measured through the volume of insurance quotes generated and the number of new policies activated from quotes.
The role is measured on quote-to-policy conversion across the funnel and NTU (not-taken-up) rates on quoted or approved policies, where lower is better.
Additional measures include persistency, which reflects the retention of active policies over time, retention across the overall portfolio, and premium growth through growth in gross written premium (GWP).
The role is also measured on campaign ROI, reflecting the return on marketing spend by campaign and channel.
What This Role Is Not
To keep commercial ownership and execution cleanly separated, this role is explicitly not responsible for:
• Campaign production or campaign loading
• Creative traffic management
• Project management and workflow management
• Campaign scheduling
• Compliance administration
• Asset managementThese responsibilities belong to the Marketing Campaign Specialist. The Marketing Manager briefs, prioritises and guides that work. It does not perform it.
Candidate Profile
We are looking for a commercially minded product marketer, not a campaign coordinator and not a Head of Marketing. Someone who is happiest with a funnel, a data set and a customer problem in front of them.
• 5–8 years' marketing experience, ideally in financial services
• Strong digital marketing capability across acquisition and lifecycle
• Hands-on CRM and customer-journey experience
• Campaign planning and briefing experience
• A commercial mindset, fluent in conversion, cost and value, not just activity
• Strong Excel and Power BI capability; comfortable interpreting data independently
• Excellent written and verbal communication
• Strong stakeholder management across commercial and technical teams
• SQL is desirable but not mandatoryLeadership Expectations
This role may not carry direct reports from day one, but it is a leadership position. We expect ownership, accountability and initiative, someone who sets the commercial agenda for their portfolio, thinks like an operator, collaborates across functions, and influences outcomes through evidence rather than authority.
How Success Is Measured
Success is measured by commercial outcomes and the quality of thinking behind them, not by campaign administration or delivery activity.
Evidence of success includes:
• Improved conversion across the funnel
• Customer growth
• Campaign effectiveness and marketing ROI
• Measurable customer-journey improvements
• Cross-sell performance
• Customer engagement and retention
• The quality of commercial recommendations made to leadership
• Stakeholder satisfaction

The Inbound Controller: Import & Export is responsible for managing and controlling the end-to-end import and export flow of goods to warehouses, distribution centers, or directly to clients. The role ensures that all shipments are executed accurately, compliantly, cost-effectively, and timeously, in accordance with SARS customs regulations, trade requirements, and company standards
Key Responsibilities
1. Pre-Shipment & Trade Coordination (Import & Export)
Liaise with international suppliers and export partners to confirm goods readiness, packaging, labelling standards, and shipping deadlines.
Verify and apply correct Incoterms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, etc.).
Book freight with approved freight forwarders across sea, air, road, and rail transport modes.
Request, validate, and manage all import and export shipping documentation prior to shipment departure.
2. Import & Export Documentation & Customs Clearance
Manage all import and export customs documentation via the internal customs management system.
Ensure customs clearance is completed prior to vessel arrival (imports) or cargo departure (exports).
Prepare, review, submit, and archive SAD500 declarations for imports and exports.
Ensure accurate preparation and compliance of export documentation, including:
Commercial invoices
Packing lists
Bills of Lading / Air Waybills / Sea Waybills
Certificates of Origin (SADC, EUR1, where applicable)
Export permits and licences (where applicable)
HS tariff classifications and customs valuation
Ensure compliance with the SARS Customs & Excise Act and applicable exchange control regulations.
Support and participate in SARS audits, inspections, and regulatory reviews.
Apply working knowledge of customs stops, border police inspections, NRCS stops, and export control requirements.
Liaise with clearing agents on inspections, queries, SAD500 amendments, and customs or invoicing discrepancies.
Update internal systems with customs clearance and shipment status.
3. Shipment Tracking & Control
Track shipments from origin to final destination.
Monitor ETD/ETA, transhipments, route changes, and delays.
Proactively communicate shipment status, risks, and delays to internal stakeholders.
Conduct daily follow-ups with clearing agents, transporters, and relevant parties.
4. Warehouse, Inventory & Delivery Coordination
Maintain accurate container and inventory control.
Coordinate the timely receiving and unloading of inbound containers.
Schedule deliveries and collections in line with operational requirements.
Process direct deliveries via the sales system.
Book deliveries upon receipt of IODs and PODs.
Verify received goods against documentation and report shortages or damages.
5. Client & Internal Support
Support internal teams and clients with import and export-related queries.
Coordinate delivery and collection dates.
Assist with shipping, customs, and sales-related queries.
Maintain professional and effective communication with all stakeholders.
Support issue resolution and escalation where required.
6. Cost Control & Performance Monitoring
Monitor and control freight costs, demurrage, detention, and storage charges.
Support cost optimisation initiatives.
Track and support KPIs, including:
On-time delivery performance
Customs clearance lead times
Import and export cost variances
Documentation and SAD500 accuracy
Tools & Systems
Customs management systems
ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, Dynamics, or similar)
Warehouse Management Systems (WMS)
Transport Management Systems (TMS)
Microsoft Word, Excel (advanced), PowerPoint, and Outlook

job_title: Sea Freight Operator / Ocean Freight Operator
about_role:
The Sea Freight Operator is responsible for the day-to-day operational handling of import and export ocean freight shipments. The role focuses on bookings, documentation, and coordination with shipping lines, agents, transporters, and internal teams to ensure efficient and compliant cargo movement for both FCL and LCL shipments.
Key Responsibilities
1. Ocean Freight Operations
Manage end-to-end sea freight operations for FCL and LCL shipments
Process import and export ocean freight files
Coordinate vessel bookings with shipping lines and NVOCCs
Monitor vessel schedules, cut-offs, rollovers, and transhipments
Track shipments to ensure timely delivery
2. Documentation Handling
Prepare, verify, and submit all required sea freight documentation, including:
Master Bill of Lading (MBL)
House Bill of Lading (HBL)
Shipping Instructions
Commercial Invoices
Packing Lists
Delivery Orders
Ensure accuracy and compliance with customs and trade regulations
Manage document amendments and corrections with relevant parties
3. Coordination & Communication
Liaise with overseas agents, shipping lines, terminals, and transporters
Coordinate with customs brokers for cargo clearance
Communicate shipment updates, ETAs, and delays to customers and internal teams
Resolve operational issues such as delays, demurrage, and detention
4. Import & Export Handling
Manage export cargo cut-offs and port gate-in timelines
Coordinate import deliveries, container tracking, and empty returns
Monitor free time and minimize demurrage and detention costs
Ensure timely cargo release and delivery order processing
5. Cost Control & Billing Support
Verify freight costs, local charges, and supplier invoices
Ensure job files are complete and ready for billing
Support finance with accurate operational data
Identify and report cost discrepancies impacting profitability
6. Systems & Compliance
Capture and update shipment data in TMS/ERP systems (e.g., CargoWise)
Utilize Trade Tech systems (RCG) where applicable
Maintain accurate shipment records and documentation
Adhere to company SOPs and compliance requirements
Support audits and reporting processes

Job Summary:
The role is responsible for identifying new business opportunities, building relationships with potential clients, driving sales growth including developing sales & marketing strategies to achieve the company's new business sales goals. This role is fully responsible for achieving the company's new business generation objectives & outcomes. The role requires a proactive approach to market research, lead generation, & closing deals to expand the company's customer base & enhance the company's market presence.
Key Responsibilities:
Business Development:
Responsible for identifying & pursuing new supply chain business opportunities in the various industrial sectors including mining, agriculture, construction, oil, gas, etc.
Analyse customer & potential clients needs & tailor solutions to meet their specific supply chain requirements.
Build a strong customer pipeline through cross selling in the mining industry & across all other industrial sectors.
Develop & sustain robust relationships with key decision-makers in prospective client organizations. Stay informed about their activities to seize opportunities as they arise.
Develop & implement robust business growth strategies/plans to attract new clients, expand the customer base & deliver the required growth margins.
Lead the sales process from initial prospecting to finalizing & closing deals.
Implement a business intelligence system targeting potential clients (input & output pricing, materials, industry trends & market conditions & customer base).
Submit accurate & timely forecasts for new business generation & for annual budgets.
Provide monthly reports comparing actual progress to forecasted targets.
Accurately assess the financial viability & conduct risk analysis of potential clients.
Consistently achieve both individual & departmental business sales targets on a monthly basis.
Client Relationship Management:
Conduct regular follow-ups & account reviews with clients to ensure the successful delivery of the company's services, customer satisfaction & identify opportunities for further sales or upselling.
Cultivate long-term relationships with new clients to ensure repeat business & client satisfaction.
Serve as the primary point of contact for new clients during the onboarding phase.
Cross-functional Collaboration:
Collaborate with internal departments such as the contracts & marketing teams to develop & improve strategic business plans.
Work closely with the Contracts team to negotiate contracts & manage customer agreements to ensure favourable terms & conditions & revenue growth.
Effectively collaborate with legal services to ensure compliance with legal requirements in the development of new contracts.
Ensure that the central repository of existing clients, potential clients, proposals & related documents are in place & maintained ensuring all data is accurate & current.
Support the development of the annual departmental budget & oversee the management of all personnel expenses
Market Intelligence, Reporting & Analytics:
Conduct market research to analyse & understand industry trends, competitor activities & to identify new markets, new customer segments & their needs.
Stay updated on supply chain industry trends, competitors, & market conditions to effectively position the company's offerings.
Participate in industry conferences, networking events, & trade shows to build company brand awareness, increase industry knowledge & generate new leads.
Proactively promote the company's comprehensive supply chain solutions to potential clients.
Track sales performance & report on key metrics (e.g., revenue, client acquisition, lead conversion rates).
Provide insights & recommendations based on market data & feedback from prospects & clients.
Proposal & Presentation Preparation:
Prepare detailed business plans, proposals, & presentations for potential clients.
Prepare & present regular reports on the status of new business generated, return on effort/investment (ROE), performance metrics, & any issues or concerns to Exco.
Develop sales reports & gather analytical data to be share with the broader team.
Team Leadership & Management:
Ensure clear communication & cooperation across the departments to resolve any operational bottlenecks & challenges.
Foster a collaborative environment across the various departments ensuring the BU achieves its financial goals & operates in compliance with applicable laws, regulations, & corporate policies.
Health, Safety & QMS:
Ensure QMS requirements are integrated into the HR department's business processes.
Ensure that all SHE policies & procedures are implemented, complied to & corrective action is taken in cases of non-compliance
Drive continuous improvement of business processes, QMS, Health & Safety.
Key Performance Indicators:
Revenue Growth (realised revenue)
Client Acquisition Rate (number of new clients acquired within a quarter)
Client Retention Rate
Lead Conversion Rate (leads converted into actual sales or contracts)
Cost of Customer Acquisition - CAC (the total cost involved in acquiring a new customer)
Market Penetration
Sales Pipeline Velocity (speed at which leads move through the sales pipeline)
Average Deal Size (in terms of revenue)
Proposal Success Rate (% proposals that result in successful deals)
Client satisfaction rate
Zero workplace safety incidents reported
Number of One-on-Ones held with General Manager

The South African National Biodiversity Institute (SANBI) is looking for a self-motivated individual to provide strategic leadership, oversight and coordination for the delivery of Component 3 of the Ecosystem-based Disaster Risk Reduction (Eco-DRR) Project. Component 3, titled "An enabling environment is created for investment in Eco-DRR through a strengthened evidence base and improved learning and knowledge management", aims to establish an evidence base to inform processes to enhance private and public sector investment in Eco-DRR; support learning, adaptive management and ultimately scaling; and contribute to ensuring a viable exit strategy for the project. The role includes oversight of the Business Development and Natural Capital Accounting programmes of work and relevant teams, quality assurance of all Component 3 outputs prior to submission as project evidence and ensuring coherence across the enabling environment and knowledge management workstreams.
This position requires a degree in Natural Sciences, Environmental Management, Social Science, Disaster Management, Development Studies, or equivalent qualification with NQF 7. This position also requires 8 years of work experience in the relevant field, 4 years of which should be in first line management position(s), including demonstrated experience overseeing complex, multi-workstream programmes or projects with diverse technical teams is essential.
The following competencies are required for the candidate to be successful in this position: technical experience in disaster risk reduction, natural resource management and evidence generation; experience in facilitating social learning processes and translating evidence and lessons into knowledge products; experience working with all spheres of government in the development, planning and implementation of policy relating to biodiversity, climate change and ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction; working knowledge of project management concepts, practices and procedures, including process development and project execution skills; and an understanding of how to work with and support communities of practice, particularly in the evidence, learning and knowledge management fields. The candidate must have excellent written and verbal English communication skills, including report writing, presentation, interpersonal and workshop facilitation skills. The ability to influence, motivate and collaborate with others is essential, as is an understanding of global and national biodiversity conservation policies and legislation. Project management skills, advanced knowledge of compliance and risk management techniques, and effective people, budget and financial management skills are also required. Familiarity with GCF or equivalent international climate fund reporting requirements, including results frameworks, annual performance reports, and mid-term and final evaluation processes, will be an advantage. The candidate must have a proven ability to work under pressure with diverse teams while remaining cost, quality and safety conscious. The ability to develop partnerships and manage multi-faceted stakeholders from various backgrounds and cultures is essential. Advanced planning, organising and problem-solving skills are required. Excellent computer literacy and experience in the application of software tools, including MS Word, MS Project, PowerPoint, Excel, Internet and Outlook, are essential. Possession of a valid driver’s licence, minimum Code B, with at least one year of practical driving experience and a willingness to travel, is essential.
Key Performance Responsibilities include:
• Provide strategic leadership, programme management and oversight of Component 3 delivery;
• Provide strategic leadership and coordination for the project's evidence, knowledge management and social learning strategy;
• Technical Leadership, Co-creation, Communication and Capacity Development;
• Provide strategic oversight for technical delivery led by the Biodiversity Information and Policy Advice Division; and
• Strengthen post-project sustainability, governance and institutional learning...........................................................................................................................................................

job_title: Key Account Manager / Field Sales Engineer
about_role:
Job Purpose
The Key Account Manager / Field Sales Engineer (KAM) is responsible for managing, retaining and growing a portfolio of key accounts by increasing sales and expanding product penetration across the customer base.
The KAM keeps customers informed of new technologies within company's (AA) line card, visits customers on a regular and planned basis, and prepares accurate, timely quotations in response to each customer request.
Success in this role depends on close collaboration across AA's internal functions.
The KAM is expected to draw on AA's engineering resources to promote new products, support design-in activity, and secure sustainable, long-term sales growth.
Key Responsibilities:
Account & Relationship Management
Establish, maintain and manage all aspects of the customer relationship, including technical support, marketing engagement and internal sales support.
Identify short-term and long-term customer needs to determine total available business potential within each account.
Develop, review and maintain account objectives and strategies, addressing customer needs and business objectives.
Strategic Account Planning & Business Development
Develop, review and update account objectives and strategies that align with both customer needs and AA's business objectives.
Proactively promote and sell AA's full product portfolio in line with marketing strategy, extending reach to all potential customers.
Proactively identify and pursue ‘design-in’ opportunities, engaging technical and engineering support as required.
Research and investigate new business opportunities, market trends and competitor activity.
Partner with AA's suppliers to initiate and drive joint customer visits to major accounts.
Sales Planning, Forecasting & Reporting
Prepare accurate sales forecasts and budgets for the assigned account portfolio.
Monthly sales reporting on call plans and MML report.
Ensure all customer negotiations are conducted within defined costing and financial parameters.
Internal Collaboration & Team Coordination
Liaise and collaborate with internal departments, effectively coordinating resources in support of account objectives.
Manage the activities of the sales administrator(s) reporting into this role to ensure effective conversion of orders into confirmed sales.
Attend and actively participate in sales and product training sessions and meetings.
Presentations & Stakeholder Engagement
Prepare and deliver presentations to existing and prospective major customers, including at senior management and director level.
Prepare and deliver presentations at internal sales meetings, reporting on progress with new and existing major accounts.
General
Undertake additional responsibilities as reasonably requested by customers or assigned by management.
Core Responsibilities:
Governance and Risk Management
Ensure ongoing compliance with applicable governance frameworks, including POPIA and ISO requirements, together with related AA policies, procedures and reporting structures.
Identify, escalate and help mitigate commercial, contractual and reputational risks arising within the account portfolio.
Maintain accurate, up-to-date and confidential customer records in line with data protection and information security requirements.
External Parties and Relationship Management
Build and sustain trusted, professional relationships with customers and suppliers that support AA's reputation as a best-in-class partner.
Represent AA professionally and consistently in all external engagements, ensuring alignment with company values and brand standards.
Communications & Working Relationships:
Purpose of Integration:
Account strategy alignment, forecasting, pipeline review and escalation of customer requirements.
Alignment on asset-related requirements and equipment supporting customer engagements.
Coordination of stock availability, delivery scheduling and order fulfilment for key accounts.
Order processing, credit terms, invoicing accuracy and resolution of account queries.
Deliver a best-in-class standard of service excellence, technical support and account management.
Joint account planning, technical collaboration and coordinated customer engagement

You don’t just react to incidents, you prevent them. By resolving deep-rooted technical challenges, mentoring teams, and ensuring compliance and security best practices, you help build confidence with clients and empower your team. Your ability to spot systemic weaknesses and correct them before they escalate directly impacts the quality, trust, and continuity of service.

• Implement, review, and enhance security measures based on threat intelligence and vendor guidance. Proactive Monitoring & Problem Prevention

• Conduct audits of system configurations, documentation, and procedures to ensure alignment with best practices and compliance standards. Mentorship, Collaboration & Leadership
• Mentor and guide Level 1 and 2 Support Engineers, providing on-the-spot coaching, structured learning sessions, and knowledge reviews.

With more than 34400 students, and approximately 1700 members of staff, the Durban University of Technology (DUT) is a leading university of technology proudly located in the beautiful cities of Durban and Pietermaritzburg, along the warm east coast of South Africa. Founded in April 2002 through the historic merger of the former ML Sultan Technikon and Technikon Natal, DUT has evolved into a modern, metropolitan, multi-campus university with roots tracing back to 1907.
Today, DUT is recognised nationally and internationally for its excellence in teaching and learning, research, innovation, entrepreneurship and engagement. A proud member of the International Association of Universities, DUT continues to expand its influence across South Africa and the world. In the 2025 Webometrics Rankings, DUT was ranked among the Top 6% of all universities and colleges worldwide, reflecting its academic excellence, research impact and strong global visibility.
DUT’s Philosophy of Education, “Our creativity and innovation shapes adaptive graduates who transform society” reflects the institution’s deep commitment to meaningful impact for societal transformation. Guided by its inspirational and aspirational ENVISION2030 strategy, which is rooted in DUT’s DNA of being ‘people-centred and engaged’ and ‘innovative and entrepreneurial’ and underpinned by its bespoke Living Values Framework, DUT focuses on ‘contributing to the improving lives and livelihoods’.
The University comprises six diverse Faculties:
• Accounting and Informatics
• Applied Sciences
• Arts & Design
• Engineering and the Built Environment
• Health Sciences
• Management SciencesDUT also includes a Business School and the award-winning Institute for Water and Wastewater Technology (IWWT), amongst other research centres and institutes, reinforcing its role as a hub for knowledge, innovation and societal impact. DUT is deeply engaged with its community and regional ecosystem, while remaining globally connected and relevant.
At DUT, we believe in nurturing talent and empowering people to make a real difference. If you are passionate about contributing to education, research, innovation, entrepreneurship and engagement, DUT offers the ideal environment - Creative. Distinctive. Impactful.

about_role:
We are looking for an energetic, sales-driven Floor Supervisor to join the Nintendo Store team at Sandton City.
This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is passionate about gaming, technology and creating memorable customer experiences. You will take ownership of daily activity on the sales floor, support the Store Manager and lead the team in achieving sales, service and operational targets.
The role is responsible for driving daily sales performance through active floor leadership, upselling and cross-selling, while ensuring that merchandising, customer experience and team execution remain aligned with Nintendo’s brand standards.
What You’ll Be Responsible For
Sales Performance
• Lead by example on the sales floor and drive the achievement of daily and monthly revenue targets.
• Actively promote cross-selling and upselling, with a strong focus on games, accessories and protection plans.
• Monitor sales performance throughout the day and adjust floor activities where required.
• Drive key sales measures, including average transaction value, units per transaction and product attachment rates.
• Support the team in converting customer traffic and product demonstrations into sales.
Floor Operations and Merchandising
• Maintain excellent floor presentation and visual merchandising standards.
• Ensure demonstration areas, interactive stations and trial products are clean, fully operational and properly stocked.
• Manage floor replenishment and ensure products are available on displays.
• Complete daily opening and closing floor checks, including point-of-sale readiness and security checks.
• Assist the Store Manager with stock counts, inventory control and shrink management.
Customer Experience
• Create an engaging, interactive and memorable experience for every customer.
• Ensure the team actively engages customers across all areas of the store.
• Respond to customer queries and resolve floor-related concerns quickly and professionally.
• Gather customer feedback and share relevant insights with the Store Manager.
• Maintain high customer satisfaction and mystery shopper standards.
Team Leadership
• Supervise, motivate and coach Retail Sales Associates and Brand Ambassadors during shifts.
• Conduct daily pre-shift meetings to communicate sales targets, promotional priorities and key products.
• Provide ongoing coaching on product knowledge, gaming titles, selling techniques and customer engagement.
• Ensure effective floor coverage and manage team rotations during busy trading periods.
• Monitor punctuality, dress code, conduct and performance.
• Address performance or behavioural concerns promptly and professionally.
• Consistently demonstrate and reinforce the company values of Focus, Passion, Innovation, Getting Things Done, Teamwork, Embracing Difference and Integrity.
What We’re Looking For
• A Higher Certificate or Diploma in Business, Retail Management, Marketing or a related field. A degree would be advantageous.
• 2 to 3 years’ experience in a high-volume retail environment.
• At least one year of experience in a supervisory, team leader or senior sales position.
• Previous experience in gaming, consumer technology, interactive retail or lifestyle brands would be highly advantageous.
• Strong sales closing, upselling and cross-selling ability.
• A genuine passion for gaming and technology.
• Strong communication, coaching and people-management skills.
• Basic knowledge of inventory management and point-of-sale controls.
• The ability to remain hands-on, energetic and customer-focused in a busy retail environment.
Why This Role?
This is an opportunity to work in an exciting, interactive retail environment where gaming, technology and customer experience come together. You will play an important role in creating the energy on the sales floor, developing the team and helping customers discover the world of Nintendo.

Purpose
To ensure the reliable, safe, and efficient operation of all standby generator systems through preventative maintenance, corrective maintenance, inspections, testing, fault diagnosis, repairs, and emergency response, thereby maximizing equipment availability and minimizing downtime.
Key Responsibilities
. Preventive Maintenance
• Perform scheduled preventive maintenance in accordance with OEM recommendations and maintenance schedules.
• Conduct routine inspections of generators, engines, alternators, radiators, fuel systems, batteries, exhaust systems, and control panels.
• Check and top up engine oil, coolant, fuel, and other consumables where required.
• Replace filters, belts, hoses, and other consumable components during scheduled services.
• Perform load bank testing and functional testing as per maintenance schedules.
• Verify operation of battery chargers, engine heaters, and auxiliary systems.
. Corrective Maintenance
• Diagnose mechanical, electrical, and control system faults.
• Carry out repairs to restore equipment to full operational condition.
• Replace defective components using approved spare parts.
• Test repaired equipment before returning it to service.
• Perform emergency breakdown repairs during and outside normal working hours when required.
. Operational Testing
• Conduct routine generator start-up and shutdown tests.
• Verify automatic transfer switch (ATS) operation.
• Confirm generator synchronisation (where applicable).
• Test emergency stop circuits and safety shutdown functions.
• Verify generator operation under simulated power failure conditions.
. Monitoring and Inspections
• Monitor generator performance through the BMS, DSEWebNet and the generator controller
• Record operating hours, alarms, warning events, and fault history.
• Inspect for oil, coolant, diesel, and exhaust leaks.
• Monitor battery condition and charging systems.
• Verify fuel levels and report any abnormalities.
. Electrical and Control Systems
• Troubleshoot Deep Sea Electronics (DSE)
• Test and replace engine protection devices, sensors, and alarms.
• Verify communication with BMS and remote monitoring platforms.
• Assist with controller programming and parameter verification where authorized and needed.
. Fuel System Maintenance
• Inspect diesel tanks, pipework, pumps, filters, and water separators.
• Inspect and Manage Diesel Bowsers
• Check for fuel contamination and water ingress.
• Coordinate fuel sampling, fuel polishing, and tank cleaning where required.
. Documentation and Reporting
• Complete maintenance reports, service sheets, and inspection checklists.
• Record equipment readings and service history.
• Report defects and recommend corrective actions.
• Provide quotations for repairs and replacement parts when required.
• Maintain accurate asset records.
. Health, Safety and Compliance
• Comply with all HSE requirements, manage work permit, and lock-out/tag-out (LOTO) procedures.
• Maintain good housekeeping in generator rooms.
• Ensure compliance with OEM specifications, SANS standards, and site safety requirements.
. Contractor and Client Support
• Supervise specialist contractors during major repairs and overhauls.
• Attend technical meetings when required.
• Assist with equipment commissioning and handover.
• Support client audits and statutory inspections.
1. Emergency Response
• After Hours Support
• Respond to generator failures.
• Restore critical standby power systems during outages.
• Provide after-hours standby support and call-out services.
Deliverables
• Completed preventive maintenance activities.
• Timely corrective maintenance and repairs.
• Accurate maintenance documentation.
• Monthly condition assessment reports.
• Recommendations for equipment replacement and lifecycle planning.
• Compliance with contractual KPIs and SLAs.
QUALIFICATIONS / REQUIREMENTS / KNOWLEDGE / SKILLS / EXPERIENCE
The Applicant must meet the following requirements:
• Grade 12 Minimum requirement
• Trade Test- Mechanical will be beneficial but not required
• Valid Code 14/ EB Driver’s License (4*4 and advanced driving will be beneficial)
• 2-3 Years’ experience in Telecommunications on GSM Sites
• Understand health and safety.
Minimum Competencies
• Diesel engine maintenance.
• Generator electrical systems.
• Automatic Transfer Switches (ATS).
• Generator synchronisation systems.
• Deep Sea Electronics (DSE) controllers or equivalent.
• Electrical fault finding.
• Mechanical fault diagnosis.
• Reading electrical schematics and wiring diagrams.
• Basic Building Management System (BMS) knowledge.
• Health and Safety compliance.
• Computer literacy and maintenance reporting systems.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

• Planned maintenance compliance ≥ 95%.

Introduction:
As the Manager: Cyber Security Operations, you are responsible for managing the day-to-day execution of cyber security operations to ensure effective monitoring, detection, response and recovery across the organisation’s technology environment.
Description:
THE JOB AT A GLANCE
As the Manager: Cyber Security Operations, you are responsible for managing the day-to-day execution of cyber security operations to ensure effective monitoring, detection, response and recovery across the organisation’s technology environment. Your role supports the Head of Cyber Security Operations in maintaining a resilient and intelligence-driven cyber defence capability that is aligned to operational priorities, risk requirements and service expectations.
Your role provides operational leadership over SOC activities, cyber incident response coordination, vulnerability remediation tracking, threat detection improvement and cyber resilience readiness. It ensures that cyber operational controls, processes and technologies are functioning effectively and that threats and incidents are addressed in a timely, controlled and well-documented manner.
Your role also serves as a key operational interface between cyber security operations and other technology and business stakeholders, enabling effective coordination during incidents, remediation programmes, audits and operational initiatives. You are accountable for team supervision, operational reporting, process improvement and continuous enhancement of cyber security operational performance.
WHAT YOU WILL DO
Security Operations Centre (SOC) & SIEM Management
• Manage the day-to-day operation of the Security Operations Centre (SOC), ensuring continuous monitoring, alert triage, investigation, and timely escalation
• Oversee the effective use of the SIEM platform, including monitoring coverage, use case execution, alert quality, and operational tuning
• Support the optimization of detection rules, use cases, and alert correlation to improve visibility and reduce false positives
• Ensure SOC procedures, playbooks, escalation paths, and service levels are consistently applied and maintained.
Cyber Incident Management & Response
• Manage operational cyber incident response processes, including detection, logging, triage, escalation, containment, eradication, recovery, and closure.
• Coordinate cross-functional response activities during cyber incidents, working with IT, Legal, Risk, and business stakeholders as required.
• Support the Head of Cybersecurity Operations during major incidents and provide operational leadership during lower to medium severity incidents.
• Facilitate post-incident reviews, root cause documentation, and tracking of lessons learned and corrective actions.
Threat Hunting & Adversary Detection
• Coordinate proactive threat hunting activities aimed at identifying hidden threats, suspicious behaviour, and advanced attack indicators
• Support the use of threat intelligence, behavioural analytics, and internal testing results to improve monitoring and detection effectiveness
• Assist with internal penetration testing, purple team exercises, and validation of detection controls
• Help refine detection use cases in response to changes in threat landscape, attack trends, and business risk.
Vulnerability & Patch Management
• Manage vulnerability scanning schedules, remediation tracking, and reporting across infrastructure, applications, cloud platforms, and endpoints
• Work with IT teams to prioritise and remediate vulnerabilities based on risk, exploitability, and business impact
• Coordinate patch management follow-up to ensure critical updates are implemented within agreed timelines
• Report on vulnerability posture, patch compliance, remediation performance, and areas of material exposure.
Cyber Resilience & Crisis Readiness
• Support the planning and execution of cyber resilience activities, including breach simulations, ransomware scenarios, and operational readiness exercises
• Coordinate operational preparedness for high-impact security incidents and support enterprise crisis response structures when invoked
• Assist in testing and validating operational response capabilities, recovery actions, and communication procedures.
Breach Containment, Recovery & Forensics
• Coordinate containment, recovery and restoration activities during cyber incidents to minimise operational disruption
• Support forensic evidence handling, investigation coordination and incident documentation in line with policy and legal requirements
• Ensure recovery actions are properly tracked, validated and closed out following incidents.
Threat Intelligence Integration
• Support the integration of relevant internal and external threat intelligence into cyber operations processes and monitoring activities
• Ensure threat intelligence is converted into practical detection improvements, watchlists, and response actions
• Maintain operational awareness of current cyber threats relevant to the organisation’s industry and environment.
Operational Reporting & Management Reporting
• Produce regular operational and management reports covering cyber incidents, SOC performance, threat activity, vulnerability exposure, remediation progress, and resilience readiness
• Track and report key performance and risk indicators such as MTTD, MTTR, dwell time, incident volumes, and remediation status
• Escalate material trends, risks, and operational issues to the Head of Cybersecurity Operations with clear analysis and recommendations
• Maintain reporting dashboards and management information to support continuous improvement and informed decision-making.
Stakeholder Management & Cross-Functional Coordination
• Work closely with IT Operations, Infrastructure, Software Development, Cybersecurity Engineering, IT GRC, Risk, and Legal teams to ensure effective operational coordination
• Act as a key operational liaison during incidents, vulnerability remediation, and cyber resilience activities
• Support alignment between cybersecurity operations processes and broader technology and business requirements.
Technology & Capability Enablement
• Support the implementation, configuration, and optimisation of security operations tooling, including SIEM, SOAR, EDR/XDR, vulnerability management, and threat intelligence platforms
• Ensure operational processes take advantage of automation and integration opportunities to improve efficiency and response speed
• Contribute to the delivery of cybersecurity roadmap initiatives relevant to operations
• Support secure onboarding and operational readiness of new platforms, cloud services, and third-party solutions.
Leadership & Capability Development
• Supervise and develop cybersecurity operations staff, including analysts and other operational resources assigned to the function
• Manage work allocation, shift coverage or operational schedules, quality of output, and adherence to procedures and SLAs
• Provide coaching, mentoring, and on-the-job development to strengthen operational capability and readiness
• Promote a culture of accountability, responsiveness, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
WHAT YOU WILL GET IN RETURN
We offer great opportunities for personal and professional development in a stable company that is 132 years strong. The role comes with a competitive salary package and various benefits. Furthermore, you will be part of a dedicated group of colleagues who value teamwork and collaboration.

PURPOSE OF THE ROLE:
The Revenue and Quality Control (QC) Clerk is responsible for ensuring the accuracy, completeness and integrity of operational revenue, customer billing, supplier costs and supporting documentation. The incumbent will perform quality control checks across operational and financial transactions to safeguard company profitability, minimise revenue leakage, validate supplier costs and ensure compliance with company policies, customer agreements and operational procedures.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
1. Revenue Quality Control:
• Verify all customer revenue prior to invoicing.
• Ensure approved customer tariffs, pricing agreements and contractual rates have been correctly applied.
• Validate freight charges against approved customer rate schedules.
• Verify actual versus volumetric weights, and confirm pallet quantities, dimensions and service types.
• Ensure fuel surcharges, documentation fees and all applicable accessorial charges have been correctly applied.
• Ensure all billable services have been accurately captured before invoices are released.
• Identify underbilling, overbilling and revenue leakage, and investigate billing discrepancies before invoicing.
• Ensure invoices are processed within agreed service level agreements (SLAs).
2. Destination and Routing Verification:
• Verify that all collection and delivery destinations have been accurately captured by Operations, Inhouse Teams and Customers.
• Ensure destination branches, delivery points, service locations and routes are correctly allocated.
• Validate that all waybills are assigned to the correct customer account, destination and service type.
• Identify and investigate incorrect destination captures that could result in operational delays, incorrect billing or misrouted freight.
• Ensure destination amendments are authorised and supported by appropriate documentation.
• Liaise with Operations, Customer Service and Customers to resolve destination discrepancies.
• Monitor recurring destination capture errors and recommend corrective actions.
3. Cost of Sales (COS):
Quality Control Primary focus on validating all Cost of Sales suppliers, including Third Party Suppliers, Linehaul Suppliers and Labour Suppliers:
• Verify supplier invoices against approved pricing agreements and contracts.
• Confirm services billed were performed and authorised.
• Validate routes, kilometres, vehicle allocations and operational activities.
• Verify labour hours and supporting documentation.
• Identify duplicate, incorrect or unauthorised supplier invoices, and resolve discrepancies before payment.
• Identify opportunities to reduce unnecessary operational expenditure.
4. Operational Invoice Verification:
Perform detailed quality control checks on all operational invoices, including freight rates, customer tariffs, supplier rates, weights, consolidations, pallet quantities, delivery zones, regional and outlying delivery charges, fuel calculations, documentation fees, insurance charges and other applicable surcharges, collection and delivery dates, Proof of Delivery (POD), duplicate billing, missing waybills, incorrect customer allocations, supporting documentation and customer purchase orders where applicable.
5. Revenue Protection:
• Identify and eliminate revenue leakage, and recover missed billable revenue.
• Ensure all operational costs are recoverable where applicable.
• Protect company profitability through accurate billing and quality control, minimising financial losses from billing inaccuracies or operational errors.
6. Reporting Prepare daily, weekly and monthly reports on revenue, billing and supplier discrepancies, QC findings, revenue recovered, cost savings identified, outstanding investigations, operational exception reports, revenue leakage analysis and supplier overcharge reports.
7. Compliance and Governance Ensure compliance with company policies, approved customer tariffs and pricing agreements, supplier contracts, operational SOPs, internal financial controls, quality standards and audit requirements. Maintain complete audit trails for all corrections, adjustments, approvals and supporting documentation.
8. Continuous Improvement:
• Identify recurring operational and billing errors and recommend process improvements.
• Assist in developing and maintaining Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
• Support continuous improvement initiatives that improve billing accuracy, operational efficiency and customer service.

Job Description: Assistant Front of House (FOH) Manager
Position Overview
• Position Title: Assistant FOH Manager
• Department: Restaurants
• Division: Hospitality Division
• Reporting To: Senior FOH Manager
• Second Level Superior: Restaurant Manager
• Direct Reports: Waitrons (17), Bartenders (4), Runners (8), Hosts (2), Reservationists (1), Events & Sales Coordinator (1)
• Salary: R15 000 – R20 000 CTC per month
Role Summary
The Assistant Front of House (FOH) Manager is responsible for overseeing and coordinating the planning, organizing, training, and leadership necessary to achieve restaurant objectives in sales, cost management, employee retention, guest satisfaction, food and beverage quality, cleanliness, and sanitation. This role focuses on maintaining exceptional operational standards while building and leading an energized, cohesive service team.
Key Result Areas & Responsibilities
1. FOH Supervision & Operations (40% Allocation)
• Ensure all food and beverage offerings are consistently prepared and served in line with luxury service standards.
• Manage staff levels, wages, shift hours, and construct FOH rosters aligned with forecasted business volume to meet labor cost targets.
• Conduct ongoing training and professional development for FOH team members.
• Inspect and maintain all front-of-house equipment in proper working condition, following preventative maintenance schedules.
• Monitor daily breakages and waste, taking appropriate action to minimize loss.
• Administer fair, consistent, and prompt corrective actions for policy or procedural violations.
• Maintain productive relationships with key operational suppliers.
2. Guest Experience & Satisfaction (30% Allocation)
• Act as the primary point of contact for customer complaints, resolving issues swiftly and professionally.
• Foster strong, long-term relationships with regular guests, estate residents, and visitors.
• Ensure every guest receives responsive, warm, and attentive service across all dining touchpoints.
3. General Operations, Administration & Compliance (10% Allocation)
• Prepare all required operational paperwork, schedules, and management reports in an organized, timely manner.
• Possess strong math skills to manage POS operations and assist with floor coverage during peak operational periods.
• Collaborate with upper management on hiring, onboarding, and termination decisions.
• Apply core leadership principles: consider the whole business, take accountability, embody professional excellence, invite feedback, and apply lessons learned.
4. Stock, Reservations & Cash Management (12% Allocation)
• Stock Control (5%): Ensure adequate ordering and stock levels for operating equipment (OE) and beverages; verify receiving counts, track beverage pricing, and manage daily stock counts and variance reports.
• Reservations (4%): Oversee host and reservationist operations using DinePlan to maximize table seating and ensure precise booking execution.
• Cash Up & Handover (3%): Control cash and digital receipts via formal reconciliation processes and record detailed daily handovers.
5. Cleaning, Health & Safety (8% Allocation)
• Health & Safety (5%): Maintain full compliance with industry health, safety, and labor regulations across the facility.
• Hygiene & Maintenance (3%): Enforce strict cleaning rosters to keep the FOH environment scrupulously clean; manage cleaning detergent inventory and safe handling protocols.

job_title: Business Process Analyst (Store Operations) - Support Office - IS & T
about_role:
Introduction:
The Business Process Analyst (Store Operations) supports the CIO’s enterprise transformation programme by analysing, standardising, and optimising store-level operational processes across TBCo’s retail and distribution network.
Description:
The Business Process Analyst (Store Operations) supports the CIO’s enterprise transformation programme by analysing, standardising, and optimising store-level operational processes across TBCo’s retail and distribution network.
This role ensures that store operations, including Sales, Receiving, Stock Control, Deliveries, Customer Service, and Facilities, are efficient, standardised, and digitally enabled, driving consistency, capacity creation, and superior customer experience across all branches.
The incumbent serves as the bridge between store operations and head office, translating strategic objectives into executable processes that simplify work, reduce waste, and improve service delivery.
Key Responsibilities
1. Process Analysis & Design
• Map and document As-Is and To-Be workflows for core store functions, including:
• Sales and Customer Service
• Goods Receiving and GRN
• Stock Control
• Deliveries and Logistics
• Cash Management and Administrative Procedures
• Store Maintenance and Compliance
• Identify operational inefficiencies, redundant activities, and non-standard practices across stores.
• Design optimised “To-Be” processes that promote standardisation, simplicity, and efficiency.
• Ensure all process models align with TBCo’s enterprise architecture, technology systems, and CIO strategy.
• Maintain updated store process documentation in the central process repository.
2. Process Optimisation & Continuous Improvement
• Apply Lean and Six Sigma methodologies to eliminate waste, reduce transaction time, and improve throughput.
• Collaborate with Store Managers and Regional Operations teams to implement best practices.
• Develop Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and store execution checklists.
• Monitor operational KPIs such as customer wait time, order fulfilment accuracy, inventory management and delivery turnaround.
• Establish continuous improvement loops to embed learning and drive operational maturity.
3. Digital & Automation Enablement
• Partner with IT, Architecture, and ERP teams to automate manual workflows (e.g., GRN capture, delivery confirmations, sales order tracking).
• Support rollout and training on digital tools and mobility solutions.
• Identify and document opportunities for RPA and workflow automation at store level.
• Support system testing, UAT, and change adoption for new digital initiatives.
• Ensure alignment of store processes with ERP, CRM, and e-commerce integrations.
4. Governance, Compliance & Risk
• Ensure store operations comply with King IV governance, POPIA, Health & Safety, and internal policies.
• Conduct operational compliance checks and audits of key store processes.
• Identify risks related to inventory handling, cash control, and data privacy, and recommend mitigations.
• Support standardisation of Delegation of Authority and store-level approval processes.
• Ensure full documentation and audit readiness of all store workflows.
5. Business Process Auditing
• Perform scheduled process audits across stores to ensure compliance with approved SOPs and standards.
• Develop and maintain operational audit templates and process risk registers.
• Analyse recurring issues and process deviations, recommending corrective and preventive measures.
• Partner with Operations, Finance, and Compliance to address findings and verify closure of audit actions.
• Report audit outcomes and improvement opportunities to the Risk Committee and CIO.
6. Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
• Work closely with Store Managers, Regional Managers, Shared Services, and Merchandise to ensure end-to-end process alignment.
• Facilitate process improvement workshops and training at store level.
• Capture on-the-ground insights to inform process design and future system enhancements.
• Support communication and change management initiatives for process rollouts.
• Act as the liaison between stores and head office to ensure operational feedback is incorporated into strategic planning.
Requirements:
• Bachelor’s Degree or Diploma in Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, or related field.
• 3–5 years’ experience in retail operations, process improvement, or business analysis.
• Experience mapping and optimising operational processes using BPMN or similar tools.
• Lean Six Sigma Yellow or Green Belt (preferred).
• Working knowledge of ERP, POS, inventory, and logistics systems (e.g., Syspro, SAP, Klipboard, Babbage).
• Experience with data analysis and dashboard tools (Excel, Power BI).

• Project Support: Support device-refresh cycles, office moves and bulk onboarding events under the direction of the Senior EUC Engineer and EUC Team Lead.Continuous Improvement
• Knowledge Contribution: Capture resolution steps in the knowledge base and surface recurring issues to the Senior EUC Engineer for root-cause attention — fixing the pattern, not just the ticket.

• CompTIA N+ and Security+ advantageous, not required.

The Sales Associate is responsible for delivering an exceptional in-showroom customer experience by converting customer visits into sales through effective product demonstration, needs analysis, and accurate order processing. The role focuses on frontline sales execution, customer service, administration, and adherence to operational standards, supporting the Store Supervisor and Showroom Manager in achieving sales and service outcomes.
What you will love doing in this role
Sales Execution & Conversion
• Actively engage customers on the showroom floor to understand their needs and convert interactions into sales.
• Demonstrate products effectively, clearly communicating features, benefits, pricing, and promotional offers aligned to the current catalogue.
• Achieve individual sales targets, conversion rates, and productivity expectations.
• Support acquisition activities, including account openings and order processing.Customer Experience
• Deliver a consistently positive, professional, and customer-focused sales experience.
• Guide customers through the full customer journey, including product selection, ordering, payments, and after-sales processes.
• Resolve basic customer queries and escalate complex issues to the Store Supervisor or Showroom Manager.
• Build customer trust through accurate information, ethical selling, and clear expectation setting.Product Knowledge & Pricing Accuracy
• Maintain strong knowledge of products, categories, pricing, and promotions.
• Ensure all selling and quoting is accurate and aligned to approved catalogues and systems.
• Stay informed of product updates, promotions, and sales initiatives.Administration & Order Processing
• Capture customer orders, documentation, payments, refunds, and credits accurately and timeously.
• Ensure all required customer documentation is complete and compliant.
• Maintain accurate records and system entries to support reporting and audits.Stock Handling & Showroom Standards
• Support basic stock handling activities, including receiving assistance, stock movement, and floor replenishment.
• Ensure products are handled with care to prevent damages.
• Maintain high standards of housekeeping, visual presentation, and merchandising on the sales floor.
• Follow stock control procedures and report discrepancies or risks.Compliance, Quality & Risk Awareness
• Adhere to all policies, procedures, quality standards, and internal controls.
• Follow cash handling procedures when processing payments, refunds, or credits.
• Participate in required training, inductions, and policy sign-offs.
• Escalate risks, errors, or non-compliance to the Store Supervisor.Teamwork & Performance Support
• Work collaboratively with team members to achieve showroom targets.
• Support promotions, campaigns, and activations as instructed.
• Be flexible in supporting operational requirements, including shifts, weekends, and public holidays.
What you’ll need to do this role
• Grade 12 / Matric (minimum requirement).
• Minimum 1 years’ retail sales experience.
• Customer-facing sales experience within a target-driven environment.
• Availability to work shifts, weekends, and public holidays.
• Homewares retail experience (advantageous).
• Clear credit and criminal record.
What we will love about you
• Customer-focused with a strong service mindset.
• Persuasive, confident, and professional communicator.
• Detail-oriented with a focus on accuracy and quality.
• Resilient, adaptable, and able to work in a fast-paced environment.
Behaviors we love
• Wow my customer
• Walk in my customers’ shoes
• Deliver on my promises
• Deliver insight-led solutions my customers need
• Treat the business as my own
• Take accountability
• Be curious, creative & explore opportunities
• Do it right & at the right time
• Play as a team
• Be helpful
• Be inclusive
• Find the fun

ROLE PURPOSE
The Solution Architect - Huawei Technologies is responsible for designing, validating and supporting the successful positioning of Huawei technology solutions across Nexio’s Data Centre, Energy and ICT opportunities. The role serves as the technical authority for Huawei FusionDC, SmartLi UPS, iCooling, OceanStor, CloudFabric and Huawei Cloud solutions, translating customer requirements into compliant, commercially viable and implementable architectures.The incumbent partners with Sales, Business Development, Huawei SA pre-sales teams, Nexio engineering, project management and customers to produce high-quality HLDs, LLDs, BoQs, tender responses and technical presentations. Solutions must meet customer outcomes, Nexio profitability expectations, POPIA, OHS, IEC and relevant NEC standards, while ensuring delivery teams have the documentation and technical sign-off required to implement successfully.
This role requires strong technical depth, disciplined documentation, consultative engagement with customers and the ability to create reusable Huawei reference architectures, internal enablement material and refresh paths that strengthen Nexio’s Huawei capability.
ROLE REQUIREMENT
• Design end-to-end Huawei solutions for RFPs, tenders, commercial estimates and client workshops.
• Produce HLDs, LLDs, BoQs and compliant technical response documents.
• Validate power, cooling, space and network requirements for FusionDC and SmartLi deployments.
• Ensure designs meet POPIA, OHS, IEC and applicable client NEC standards.
• Partner with BDMs and Sales to facilitate Huawei technical workshops, demos and client presentations.
• Lead PoCs, demonstrations and lab validation in Nexio DC labs.
• Provide competitor positioning and analysis for Huawei against Vertiv, Eaton, Cisco and Dell alternatives.
• Hand over approved designs to Nexio Project Managers and Engineers with clear implementation guidance.
• Provide technical sign-off and issue resolution support during implementation.
• Create reference architectures, standard build packs and repeatable design artefacts for Nexio Huawei solutions.
• Engage Huawei SA pre-sales, R&D and HQ teams for complex solution designs and escalations.
• Maintain Huawei certifications, lab access and current knowledge of the Huawei solution portfolio.
• Provide product-gap feedback and roadmap requests to Huawei.
Additional Information:
• Individuals at this level have fully developed knowledge of the business, marketplace and clients. Is recognised as an expert in own area within the organization
• Interprets internal or external business issues and recommends best practices. Provides technical guidance to more junior levels of staff
• Able to build strong interpersonal relationships with peers, brand leaders, and other senior management throughout the company
• Able to be a “big picture” thinker
• Encouraging to team and staff; able to mentor and lead
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills
• Able to align multiple strategies and ideas
• Confident in producing and presenting work
• In-depth understanding of the IT and Telecommunications industry
TECHNICAL / PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES
• Strong technical documentation, architecture presentation and stakeholder management skills.
• Ability to validate data centre power, cooling, space, network, storage and cloud design dependencies.
• Commercial awareness to support accurate BoQs, licensing, assumptions, exclusions and cost-effective solution design.
• Competence in facilitating PoCs, demos, lab validations and technical workshops.
• Understanding of POPIA, OHS, IEC and customer NEC compliance considerations.
• Ability to work under pressure, manage multiple opportunities and meet proposal timelines.
QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
• Matric and a relevant Information Technology, Engineering or equivalent qualification.
• 2-5 years’ experience in Solution Architecture, Pre-Sales, Data Centre Engineering or related technical design roles.
• Hands-on experience with at least two Huawei portfolio areas: FusionDC, UPS5000/SmartLi, iCooling, OceanStor, CloudFabric or Huawei Cloud.
• Technical knowledge across data centre power, cooling, networking, storage, virtualisation and BMS/DCIM environments.
• Huawei HCIP/HCIE certification preferred; PMP, VCP or CDCP certifications will be advantageous.
• Experience with NEC3/NEC4 contracts, BoQ responses, hyperscale/colo data centre design, Python or Ansible automation will be advantageous.

• Strong understanding of IT technologies and appropriate industry knowledge

They ensure compliance with labour legislation and company policies, provide guidance to management on people-related matters, and develop initiatives that enhance employee engagement, retention, and organisational performance.
The HR Manager works closely with leadership to align HR strategies with business objectives while creating a positive and high-performing work environment.

·       Lead and manage the full Human Resources function across the business.
·       Manage all labour relations matters, including CCMA cases, disciplinary hearings, grievances, investigations, incapacity, and retrenchments.
·       Ensure compliance with all South African labour legislation, company policies, and HR best practices.
·       Provide legal HR advice and practical solutions to management on complex employee relations matters.
·       Develop, implement, and enforce HR policies and procedures, with expert knowledge of employment legislation.
