job_title: Paarl Code A 150cc Motorbike Delivery Driver
about_role:
Paarl Code A 150cc Motorbike Delivery Driver
Are you a reliable and experienced rider with an excellent eye for detail? A well-established automotive logistics operation is looking for a dependable Code A Motorbike Delivery Driver to join their dynamic team for a full-time position.
If you take pride in road safety, possess great riding skills, and thrive in a fast-paced environment, this is your opportunity to ensure seamless, safe, and on-time parts distribution to workshops and clients.
What’s on Offer?
- Salary: R7,845.00 Gross PM
- Status: Permanent following a successful 3-month probation period
- Benefits (Post-Probation): MICFA Provident Fund (7.5% employee / 8% employer contribution) + Prorated December Annual Bonus
- Leave: 18 days paid annual leave per annum
- Hours: Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00 | Sat 08:00–13:00 (Overtime paid per MIBCO regulations)
Key Responsibilities
- Order Dispatch & Delivery: Safely transport and deliver automotive parts and components to workshops and clients within designated areas.
- Route Planning & Efficiency: Plan delivery routes effectively to ensure timely distribution while maintaining fuel efficiency and road safety.
- Verification & Documentation: Double-check delivery items against invoices/delivery notes before departure and obtain proper customer signoffs.
- Vehicle Maintenance & Care: Conduct daily pre-trip inspections of the company motorbike (oil, tyres, brakes) and keep the vehicle clean.
- Logistics Support: Assist the warehouse team with loading, securing cargo, and sorting delivery batches when not out on the road.
Are You the Perfect Fit?
Minimum Requirements & Legal Qualifications:
- Licencing: Valid, unendorsed South African CODE A DRIVER'S LICENCE IS STRICTLY REQUIRED.
- Essential Experience: Previous commercial motorbike delivery or courier experience in any industry is strictly required (automotive or logistics sector experience is a distinct advantage).
- Skills & Education: Matric certificate (highly advantageous), basic computer literacy, and the ability to navigate routes efficiently using maps or GPS.
- Track Record: High reliability, punctuality, strong road safety awareness, and a stable history with contactable references.
Strict Legal Requirements & Assessments (Non-Negotiable):
Background screening will be conducted. Candidates must have:
- South African-born Citizenship (with valid SA ID).
- Clear criminal record (under no circumstances will candidates with a record be considered).
- Ability to undergo a psychometric/personality assessment during the interview stage.
How to Apply
Ready to drive your career forward? Ensure you have the following documentation ready:
- Detailed CV (with contactable references clearly showing your motorbike delivery history).
- Licence Copy (Clear copy of your valid Code A licence).
- ID Copy (Proof of SA-born citizenship).
- Matric Certificate / Qualifications.
Apply Now: Visit https://www.easternpersonnel.co.za/ and click on Register CV.
Please Note: Only shortlisted candidates who meet all requirements, will be contacted. If you do not hear back within two weeks, please consider your application unsuccessful. Eastern Personnel is fully POPIA compliant, and all personal information will be processed securely and solely for recruitment purposes.

Introduction to the VKB Group
The VKB Group is an agricultural company, providing support to farmers and producing straight-from-the farm-foods for consumers. Apart from the various consumer brands, the VKB Group is also represented by its regional brands: VKB, GWK and NTK. Our roots are firmly planted in agriculture with farming at our core, continuously growing and evolving throughout the years.
Starting with providing everything needed on the farm to produce food, we now also operate in all areas of the food supply chain: processing, logistics, and national and global market channels.
This “house of brands” we’ve established with the support of our farmer shareholders is the foundation for building the agribusiness of the future.

Touch lives – for the better: We always aim to make a positive impact in people’s lives: our employees, producers, clients, communities and the larger industry. We do what is right, even if it scares us

We consider our words and actions

No-one can do this alone
Our legacy
For the Love of the Land: We do it all for our legacy and the love of nature, people, country, sustainability and progress.

All academics are responsible for disseminating knowledge (teaching and learning), creating knowledge (research), and engaging in community engagement, recognising differences in executing these responsibilities within the various departments and faculties. The University of the Free State (UFS) is a research-led, student-centred and regionally engaged institution committed to academic excellence, inclusivity, social justice and innovation.  Applications are invited from visionary, strategic and accomplished leaders for the position of Director: Institutional Change, Social Justice and Universal Access.
Reporting to the Deputy Vice-Chancellor: Strategic Initiatives, Internationalisation and Institutional Affairs, the successful candidate will provide strategic leadership to the Institute for Institutional Change, Social Justice and Universal Access and will champion the University's transformation agenda by promoting diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility, institutional culture and social justice across all campuses.
This executive leadership position provides a unique opportunity to influence institutional strategy, advise Executive Management and governance structures, and position the University of the Free State as a national leader in institutional transformation, universal access and inclusive excellence.
The Director is responsible for providing strategic leadership and executive oversight of the Institute for Institutional Change, Social Justice and Universal Access by developing, implementing and evaluating institutional strategies, policies and programmes that advance transformation, diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility, universal access, institutional culture and human rights.

•    Ensure compliance with applicable higher education legislation, governance frameworks and reporting requirements.
•    Build strategic partnerships with government, higher education institutions, professional bodies, community organisations and international partners.
•    Represent the University nationally and internationally on matters relating to institutional transformation, accessibility and social justice.
•    Lead the operational, financial and people management functions of the Institute.

•    Experience advising executive leadership.
•    Experience leading multidisciplinary teams.
•    Demonstrated experience in institutional governance.
•    Extensive experience in policy development.
•    Experience leading complex strategic institutional projects.

Representing a diverse portfolio of the world’s leading passenger, commercial, and emerging electric vehicle brands, our client's dealerships offer an all-inclusive motoring solution—encompassing new and pre-owned vehicle sales, finance and insurance (F&I) services, specialized workshops, aftermarket performance tuning, and genuine parts procurement. On behalf of our client, we are seeking a meticulous, accurate, and experienced General Ledger Clerk to join their finance team.
If you have a strong background in accounting principles, a sharp eye for detail, and solid hands-on experience within the motor industry, this is an excellent opportunity to advance your career. You will play a pivotal role in maintaining core financial records, performing account reconciliations, ensuring data accuracy, and supporting month-end close procedures.

Working Hours & Environment
- Standard Hours: Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00.

- Standard Working Procedures (SWP): A standard working procedures manual must be obtained from HR for your position; it must be read, signed, and returned to HR within your first week of employment.
Key Responsibilities
- Transaction Posting: Accurately post daily financial transactions and routine journal entries into the accounting system.
- Account Reconciliations: Perform complete monthly reconciliations for assigned general ledger accounts.
- Error Investigation: Proactively investigate, troubleshoot, and resolve accounting errors or data mismatches.
- Audit Support: Prepare and compile detailed supporting documentation for internal and external audits.
- Period Closing: Assist the financial team with month-end and year-end closing tasks according to set timelines.
Requirements & Qualifications
- Experience: Proven, stable experience as a General Ledger Clerk within the Motor Sector is strictly essential and non-negotiable.
- Bookkeeping Knowledge: Strong, practical grasp of basic bookkeeping principles and accounting workflows.
- Systems Knowledge & Skills: Advanced proficiency with spreadsheets (MS Excel) and financial/accounting software.

• Ensure that ANY horses you are handling/working- or coming into contact with whilst on Academy grounds has access to ample clean water to drink.
• Ensure EVERY safety precaution is taken to facilitate the safety of any horse, handler, rider, bystanders and any other horses in the immediate surrounding vicinity at all times, whilst handling/working- or coming into contact with, whilst on Academy grounds.

• Responsibly handling, using & packing away of ANY & All horse tack belonging to or being utilized by WEA.
• Maintenance (cleaning and oiling as and when required) of saddles, girths, surcingles, bridles, brushing boots, lunging equipment, numnahs, grooming kits ect.

• Schooling of horses as per WEA’s requirements

• Show turn out and show assistance as per WEA requirements
• Weekend duties as per protocol, and/or determined by the Academy Manager.

As such you are expected to behave within the guidelines of The Academy’s image.

We’ve got a position available for a junior actuarial analyst
Company: Porcupine Union, part of the King Price Group
Purpose of position:
The Junior Actuarial Analyst supports our pricing and rating work: building and maintaining the models that determine what our clients charge, deriving and testing rating factors, and running the analyses that show whether a rate is adequate. Alongside that core, the role contributes to predictive modelling and general analytical work as demand requires.
Responsibilities:
Pricing and rating (core focus)
• Assist in building, maintaining and testing pricing models for insurance and other client products.
• Analyse claims and exposure experience to derive and validate rating factors and relativities.
• Build and maintain rating tables and rating structures; test them for correctness before they go live.
• Run rate reviews, rate adequacy assessments, sensitivity tests and scenario analyses under the guidance of senior colleagues.
• Investigate the profitability of segments within a book and flag where rates appear inadequate or uncompetitive.
• Support the implementation and testing of rating logic in client systems, including reconciling model output against system output.
• Monitor how rates perform after implementation and contribute to periodic experience reviews.
• Document model logic, assumptions, rating bases and limitations so that work is reviewable and repeatable.Predictive modelling and data science:
• Extract, clean and structure data from client systems and internal sources.
• Build and test predictive and statistical models (for example propensity, retention, claims or collections models) under supervision.
• Assess model performance and help monitor deployed models for drift and deterioration.
• Contribute to the automation of recurring analysis so that manual effort is reduced over time.General analytical support and delivery:
• Turn around ad hoc analytical requests from internal teams and clients accurately and on time.
• Produce clear tables, charts and short written summaries that a non-technical reader can act on.
• Investigate data quality issues and flag them, with a proposed course of action, rather than working around them silently.
• Support senior colleagues in preparing client-facing material and in meetings.Requirements:
• A completed (or final-year) Bachelor’s degree in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Econometrics or a closely related quantitative field.
• Strong academic record in quantitative subjects.
• Demonstrable ability to write code for data analysis in Python or R — through coursework, projects, internships or self-directed work.
• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
• Sound written and verbal communication in English, including the ability to explain a technical result to a non-technical audience.
• Able to work from our Pretoria office.
• 0–2 years’ work experience. Graduates with no formal work experience are welcome to apply.Skills and attributes:
• Analytical rigour — checks their own work, understands why a number is what it is, and is uncomfortable presenting a result they cannot explain.
• Intellectual honesty — says when they are unsure or when they have made an error; does not defend a result they no longer believe.
• Curiosity and independent thinking — asks why the conventional approach is the right one, and is willing to voice a different view.
• Learning agility — picks up unfamiliar techniques and tools quickly and applies them without extensive hand-holding.
• Ownership and reliability — delivers what was agreed, on time, and communicates early when something is at risk.
• Collaboration — works well within a small, busy team and shares knowledge rather than hoarding it.
• Clear communication — translates technical work into language a commercial audience can use.

Millwright-Cape Winelands
Looking for a trade-tested Millwright to maintain, fault-find, repair and continuously improve the mechanical and electrical equipment throughout our MegaPlant.
This is a hands-on factory-floor role for someone highly efficient, technically proficient, dependable and able to work independently.
We are looking for an artisan who finds the root cause of failures, not someone who simply replaces failed components
Requirments:
• Trade Test Millwright 5–10+ years relevant post-trade experience
• Industrial/Manufacturing maintenance experience.
• Strong mechanical and electrical fault-finding ability.
• Able to work efficiently with minimal supervision.
• Able to read mechanical and electrical drawings.
• Strong practical problem-solving ability.
• High standard of workmanship and safety.
• Comfortable working in a heavy industrial factory environment.
Strong experience with:
• Motors, gearboxes, bearings and couplings.
• Shaft, pulley and drive alignment.
• Conveyors, belts, chains and sprockets.
• Crushers, screens, mixers and production machinery.
• Pumps, fans and rotating equipment.
• Hydraulics and pneumatics.
• Fabrication and welding.
• Three-phase electrical systems.
• MCCs, contactors and overloads.
• Variable Speed Drives (VSDs).
• Sensors, limit switches and interlocks.
• Basic PLC fault finding and PLC I/O.
• Automated production equipment.
Key Responsibilities
• Respond rapidly and efficiently to production breakdowns.
• Diagnose mechanical, electrical, control and process-related faults.
• Identify and correct the root cause of failures.
• Carry out preventative and planned maintenance.
• Inspect machinery proactively and identify developing problems.
• Ensure correct bearing installation, alignment, lubrication and equipment mounting.
• Test equipment properly before returning it to production.
• Record significant failures and corrective actions.
• Identify critical spare-part requirements.
• Support shutdowns and major maintenance work.
Continuous Improvement
• Our Millwrights are expected to improve the factory, not simply maintain it.
• They should actively identify opportunities to:
• Reduce repetitive breakdowns.
• Increase plant availability and production throughput.
• Reduce maintenance costs.
• Improve equipment reliability.
• Improve electrical and mechanical efficiency.
• Reduce unnecessary motor loading and power consumption.
• Improve guarding, safety and maintainability.
• Improve sensors, controls and automation.

job_title: Head of Amazon Advertising & Performance Marketing
about_role:
Head of Amazon Advertising & Performance Marketing
Location: Remote (Preference for Western / Western-aligned time zones)
Type: Full-Time
Reports to: CEO
Compensation: Top-decile base + aggressive profit-based upside
The Role – In One Sentence
You are the money engine on Amazon.
You own every dollar that comes in the door through Amazon PPC/DSP and retail media — and you know exactly how to turn ad spend into profitable, compounding growth. No excuses, no "seasonality," no "the algorithm changed."
Amazon is your home field. Other channels are tools you wield to support it.
First 90 Days – Non-Negotiable Outcomes
If this doesn't excite you as a challenge, this isn't your role.
• Full Amazon Audit – Nothing Unchecked
• Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Display, DSP
• Campaign structure, keyword targeting, audience segmentation, placements
• Listing quality: titles, bullets, images, A+ content, reviews, pricing, bundles
Result: full teardown with clear kill/scale/rebuild plan.
• New Testing Machine Live (Amazon-First)
• Minimum 20 new tests/week across: keywords, bids, creatives, angles, funnels, audiences
• Systematic framework for A/B testing and rapid iteration
• Clear "what we test / why we test / how we decide" playbook
• Amazon Profitability Benchmarks Hit or Clearly Tracked Toward
• Target TACoS, ACOS, and blended ROAS defined and tracked
• Path to 3.5x+ blended ROAS across Amazon
• $50k+/month in controlled, profitable ad spend (or ready to scale to that level sustainably)
• Founder Independence
• Zero reliance on the CEO for copy, angles, hooks, or approvals
• You bring the ideas, tests, and decisions — Founder stays in vision and product, not ads. What You Own
You are Head of Amazon Ads, but you understand the whole growth ecosystem.
Amazon – Your Core Battlefield
• Amazon PPC: Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Display
• Keyword research, search term mining, and negative keyword strategy
• Campaign architecture (structure for scale, not chaos)
• Bid strategies (down-only, up/down, fixed bids, placement adjustments)
• TACoS/ACOS optimization and margin protection
• Launch strategy for new products, variants, and bundles Conversion & Creative
• Listing optimization: titles, bullets, imagery, A+ content, brand store
• Review strategy, social proof, and UGC alignment with Amazon page assets
• Creative strategy for Amazon ads (thumbnails, video, lifestyle, comparison ads)
• Angle and hook testing: performance-driven storytelling specifically for Amazon shoppers Cross-Channel Support (Performance Marketing)
• Using TikTok selectively where they support Amazon growth
• LTV/CAC modeling across channels with Amazon as the core revenue driver Measurement & Economics
• LTV/CAC and payback windows on Amazon-first journeys
• Blended ROAS across Amazon and supporting channels
• Reporting that the CEO can scan in 5 minutes and know exactly what's working You don't just "run ads." You design the acquisition system that scales profitably.
Mandatory Prerequisites – No Exceptions
We will check. This is not a "figure it out as you go" seat.
• You have personally scaled Amazon advertising profitably for a CPG/supplement or similar product brand.
• Not agency "I advised" fluff. Actual ownership of P&L outcomes.
• You can point to real brands, real spend, real results.
• You have taken a brand from weak returns (under 2x ROAS / unprofitable TACoS) to strong performance (4x+ ROAS or materially improved TACoS) in under 6–9 months.
• Before/after numbers and what you changed.
• You still run accounts yourself.
• No "I just manage the team now" distance.
• You're in the platforms, making decisions, and testing ideas.
• You can look at a search term report, listing, or ad creative and have a strong POV in under 30 seconds.
• Pattern recognition from heavy reps, not vibes. How You'll Be Judged
This is a scoreboard role. You will live and die by the numbers:
• Blended ROAS across Amazon and supporting channels
• Amazon TACoS and ACOS by product line
• New customer CAC (Amazon-first and blended)
• Margin after ad spend (not just top-line hero screenshots)
• Speed of learning – a new winning angle or structure every 7–14 days If you need "more time" and "more budget" before you can show results, this will be a painful role. If you love moving fast and pressure-testing your ideas, you'll thrive.
How to Apply
Send your CV + a short Loom video.
In your Loom (5–7 minutes), answer:
• Biggest Amazon (or Amazon-led) turnaround you've ever led — what was the monthly spend, TACoS/ROAS before vs. after, and what levers you pulled.
• Current training routine + proof you live it — show us how you train, compete, or otherwise live the athlete lifestyle.
• One Amazon angle, structure, or campaign strategy you'd test for a fast-growing supplement/CPG brand tomorrow — and why. This is not a "VP of Marketing" vanity title.
This is the Head of Amazon Growth in a brand that intends to dominate its category and expects its acquisition leader to think — and operate — like an owner.
Apply only if you're ready to own the numbers end to end.
I also swapped the × symbols for plain x, since those are the next most likely thing a form chokes on.

We are seeking a Detail-Oriented Controller for our Vehicle Stock department at Ford Kempton Park. In this key role, you will focus on managing inventory processes, ensuring accurate record-keeping, and optimizing stock levels to support our operations and sales goals.

- Demonstrable experience in inventory management or stock control, preferably within the automotive industry.

- Excellent organizational skills to manage multiple tasks and priorities effectively.

- A detail-oriented mindset and a commitment to maintaining high levels of accuracy.
Preferred Qualifications
- Relevant qualifications in supply chain management, logistics, or a related field.
- Experience with automotive stock management systems will be an advantage.
- Familiarity with regulatory requirements related to vehicle inventory management.
- Certification in project management or inventory control is a plus.
We are committed to creating a diverse environment and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all individuals regardless of their backgrounds, in line with the Employment Equity Act.

Reports To Head of Finance
PURPOSE OF THE ROLE:
To lead the company's procurement function: manage the sourcing, purchasing, contracting and supplier-performance cycle in line with the approved procurement procedure, financial controls, budgets and Head of Finance/Group Operations Director instructions.
The Procurement Manager is the primary point of contact between the company and its suppliers of goods, services and capital items, and is accountable for cost-effective, quality-assured and timely procurement that supports manufacturing output.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Manage purchases and costs in accordance with financial controls, procurement procedures, approved budgets and board / Group instructions.
Cultivate and maintain good working relationships with suppliers, service providers and contractors.
Resolve vendor or contractor grievances and claims against suppliers.
Review the selected strategic suppliers / service providers on their supply, delivery and pricing, in accordance with prescribed procurement procedures.
Negotiate costs and best pricing for purchases made, whilst ensuring quality of goods and services procured.
Maintain and update the Approved Suppliers List (ASL) and their certification / accreditation, delivery times, and potential future development.
Work with all Heads of Department to prioritise procurement of supplies effectively and timeously against the production plan.
Represent the Company and annually review suppliers' agreements or contracts to ensure compliance to contracts, terms of supply and company policies.
Develop and implement purchase and contract management instructions, policies and procedures.
Participate in the development and specifications for equipment, products or substitute materials where applicable, in conjunction with engineering and production.
Maintain the integrity of the financial / ERP accounting system (e.g. Evolution) in terms of pricing, costing and supplier terms.
Ensure the storeroom is sufficiently stocked with minimum stock levels as per agreed levels, and that replenishment is planned and ordered in good time.
Prepare, issue and adjudicate Requests for Quotation (RFQs) and Requests for Proposal (RFPs) for both local and international supply;
Manage import and export logistics, customs clearance (SARS), foreign-exchange exposure and cross-border supplier compliance (including inbound and outbound documentation, certificates of origin and SADC / EU / Asia origin rules);
Evaluate quotations on price, quality, BBBEE, lead-time and total cost of ownership; recommend awards within the delegation of authority.
Compile and submit weekly and monthly procurement reports to the Group Operations Director: spend, cost-savings, supplier performance, open POs and aged creditors.
Drive continuous improvement of the procurement function: cost-savings initiatives, supplier-development programmes, process automation and full compliance with the Business Management System,
AUTHORITY:
Recommend and approve supplier awards, contract renewals and Approved Suppliers List additions/removals within the procurement delegation of authority; escalate to the Group Operations Director as required.
Authority to instruct the staff responsible for inventory counts to perform re-counts if necessary.
Authority to manage import / export logistics, customs clearance, foreign-exchange transactions and cross-border supplier compliance within the procurement delegation of authority; escalate material FX exposure and customs disputes to the Group Operations Director.
Recommend and approve inventory adjustments, strategic sourcing decisions and supplier development support within the delegation of authority; escalate to the Group Operations Director as required.
To Identify and report potential risks and opportunities in accordance with the Company's ERMF policy. Report proposals to Group Operations Director

about_role:
About Wholechain
Wholechain is a supply chain traceability platform that makes product journeys transparent,
helping responsible businesses meet regulatory, customer, and sustainability expectations. Built
on global data standards such as GS1 and GDST, Wholechain supports complex,
multi-commodity supply chains across food, agriculture, and consumer goods industries. The
platform enables interoperable, event-based, and lot-level traceability across suppliers,
processors, distributors, logistics providers, retailers, foodservice operators, and certification
bodies worldwide.
Wholechain helps organizations capture, share, and validate critical supply chain data across
sourcing, transformation, shipping, receiving, and production events. By creating a connected
digital chain of custody, businesses can improve food safety, strengthen recall readiness, verify
sourcing claims, meet ESG and sustainability goals, and comply with evolving regulatory
frameworks such as FDA FSMA 204 and international traceability requirements.
The platform is designed for enterprise scalability and integration, supporting APIs, EDI
workflows, ERP integrations, and interoperability with external traceability and certification
ecosystems. Wholechain works closely with industry groups, standards organizations, seafood
and agriculture partners, retailers, and global suppliers to simplify traceability adoption without
requiring all participants to use the same internal systems.
In addition to regulatory compliance, Wholechain enables businesses to build trust and
operational visibility throughout their supply networks. Customers use the platform to manage
traceability programs, verify certified products, monitor supply chain integrity, support
responsible sourcing initiatives, and provide transparent product histories to downstream buyers
and consumers.

Frogfoot is in search of a Regional Community Relations Officer for the Gauteng area.
Purpose of the Role
The Regional Community Relations Officer (RCRO) serves as Frogfoot's primary representative within Rise communities within a designated region and acts as the critical link between Frogfoot, community stakeholders, local government structures and residents.
The role is responsible for building trust, supporting fibre deployment activities, identifying and mitigating community-related risks, promoting digital inclusion and driving fibre adoption through effective stakeholder engagement.
The RCRO will work closely with contractors, operations, sales, marketing and other partners to ensure that community interests are understood and incorporated into rollout plans while supporting Frogfoot's commercial and social impact objectives.
The ideal RCRO is someone who is equally comfortable speaking with a ward councillor, school principal, community activist, informal trader or senior Frogfoot executive. They combine strong relationship-building skills with operational discipline and have a genuine passion for expanding digital access and economic opportunity within South African communities.
What You’ll Be Responsible For
Community Engagement & Relationship Management
• Build and maintain strong relationships with:
• Ward councillors, Community leaders, Community Policing Forums (CPFs), Residents' associations, Schools and educational institutions, Faith-based organisations, Local NGOs and NPOs, Youth organisations, Business forums and informal trader associations.
• Serve as Frogfoot's first point of contact within assigned communities.
• Conduct regular stakeholder meetings and community engagement sessions.
• Facilitate community information sessions before, during and after network deployment.
• Represent Frogfoot at community forums and public meetings.Rollout Support & Community Risk Management
• Coordinate and conduct physical roll-out feasibility assessments in new and existing areas, providing key insights and inputs in due diligence supporting roll-out.
• Support network rollout activities by ensuring effective community communication.
• Identify potential community-related risks that may impact project delivery, including community resistance, political interference, protests and unrest, vandalism and theft, and access challenges
• Develop mitigation plans in collaboration with operational teams.
• Monitor community sentiment and escalate emerging issues to the Head of Community Relations.
• Assist in resolving disputes relating to construction activities and network deployment.Community Intelligence & Reporting
• Maintain an accurate stakeholder database for assigned regions.
• Gather and analyse community intelligence relating to sentiment towards Frogfoot, adoption barriers, community concerns and local economic opportunities
• Provide weekly and monthly reports highlighting engagement activities, community risks, stakeholder feedback, escalations and resolutions
• Maintain records of all stakeholder interactions.
• Oversee community outreach campaigns to educate and promote the benefits of fibre connectivity.
• Design and implement conflict resolution frameworks to address disruptions during rollout.
• Support adoption campaigns by working closely with retail partners in communities.Fibre Adoption & Digital Inclusion
• Support community education initiatives aimed at increasing awareness of fibre services.
• Collaborate with retail partners and sales teams to promote fibre adoption.
• Participate in community activation campaigns.
• Identify opportunities to support digital literacy programmes, community Wi-Fi initiatives, educational partnerships and local entrepreneurship initiatives
• Assist in measuring the social impact of Frogfoot's presence within communities.What You’ll Need to Have
Qualifications
• Qualification in Community Development, Public Relations, Communications, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Public Administration or Related field.Experience
• 3-5 years of experience in community relations, stakeholder engagement or corporate social investment (CSI/CSR).
• Experience working with diverse communities.
• Experience managing multiple stakeholders simultaneously.
• Experience in telecommunications, utilities, infrastructure rollout, social development programmes or related industries is highly advantageous. Skills That Will Help You Succeed
• Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills.
• Strong negotiation, mediation and conflict resolution skills.
• Ability to engage effectively at grassroots (community forums) level.
• Fluency in English and at least one South African indigenous language (isiZulu, isiXhosa, Sesotho, Setswana preferred).
• Comfortable with extensive travel to communities.
• Community intelligence gathering.
• Risk identification and mitigation. Qualities We Value at Frogfoot
At Frogfoot, we look for people who are:
• Build trust and credibility across diverse stakeholder groups.
• Demonstrates sensitivity to different social, cultural, and economic contexts.
• Communicates effectively with both grassroots stakeholders and corporate teams.
• Proactively identifies issues and develops practical solutions.
• Remains calm and effective in challenging and politically sensitive situations.
• Takes ownership of community-related outcomes.How Success Is Measured
Success in this role will be measured by your ability to:
• Stakeholder Engagement.
• Community Mapping.
• Risk Management.
• Issue Resolution.
• Community Sentiment.
• Adoption Support.
• Community Partnerships.

The Civil Engineer provides oversight of civil infrastructure across the 128-site South Africa portfolio. The position is responsible for the structural integrity, inspection, maintenance planning, and standards compliance of all civil works — elevated reinforced-concrete reservoirs, tank towers, distribution networks, standpipes, pump houses, borehole chambers, cattle troughs, and solar frame structures — and for coordinating specialist chartered engineering inspections of high-capacity 30-kilolitre tank-class infrastructure in accordance with applicable SANS standards.
The role is central to the Year 1 technical condition assessment of all 128 sites, the site-tier triage (A/B/C), the remediation of named Tier C sites, and the drawdown planning of the Replacement Capex Reserve for civil components.
3. Key Responsibilities
3.1 Technical condition assessment and site-tier triage (Year 1)
• Lead the civil and structural component of the site-by-site technical condition assessment across all 128 South African sites within the first three months of the programme (Stream B of the Day 1 transition), covering tanks, towers, distribution networks, valves and fittings, pump houses, and civil structures.
• Contribute civil condition data to the site-tier triage (Tier A/B/C) to be confirmed by Month 3 and identify civil components requiring Day 1 or Year 1 replacement funded from the Replacement Capex Reserve.
• Support full condition assessment and Tier C remediation at the named priority sites, including Jabulani and the five untested Mpumalanga sites (Igliton Hotel Section, Igliton Mdluli Section, Mihlanguleni, Rhandzekile A, Rhandzekile B), under the 48-hour remediation initiation protocol.
• Verify and reconcile the civil elements of the Innovation: Africa handover package, including as-built and structural drawings (3m, 7m, and 10m tank towers; the 30-kilolitre high-capacity tank class), borehole completion reports, and site asset registers.3.2 Routine civil inspection and maintenance oversight (Years 1-3)
• Design and implement the routine structural inspection cycle for civil infrastructure across the portfolio, integrated into the Tier 2 quarterly inspection programme (structural inspection of concrete towers, reservoirs, and distribution infrastructure).
• Procure, scope, and supervise specialist-chartered engineering inspections of 30-kilolitre reinforced-concrete tanks in compliance with applicable SANS standards, managing the specialist sub-contract and certifying deliverables.
• Develop civil maintenance specifications, bills of quantities, and scopes of work for repairs, rehabilitation, and upgrades; supervise contractors and certify completed works.
• Assess and prioritise Parent-site civil infrastructure within the cluster maintenance model, recognising that a Parent borehole failure cascades to hydraulically dependent Child sites (56 Child sites in South Africa).
• Support reactive repair response for civil failures in line with the tiered service-impact protocol (critical failures within 48 hours; reduced-service issues within five working days).3.3 Standards compliance, quality assurance and reporting
• Ensure all civil works, inspections, and rehabilitation comply with applicable SANS standards and relevant national and municipal regulations, and that water infrastructure supports compliance with SANS 241:2015 water quality requirements.
• Maintain the civil asset register, structural inspection records, drawings library, and defect logs within the programme's field management system.
• Contribute civil infrastructure data and analysis to monthly cluster reports, quarterly donor reports to Donor, and the MEAL dashboard (KPI Categories 1 and 2: sustained service delivery and technical compliance).
• Support the DMEAL team with means-of-verification documentation for infrastructure-related KPIs.3.4 Capacity building and transition
• Train ForAfrika field engineers, community pump attendants, and Water Management Committee members in basic civil infrastructure surveillance (visual inspection of tanks, towers, standpipes, and soakaways) as part of the Tier 1 community operator curriculum.
• Contribute civil O&M content to site-level O&M manuals, sustainability plans, and handover documentation supporting the Year 3 transition to community and Water Services Authority management.
• Advise on civil aspects of Capital Sinking Fund calibration, aligning contribution rates to civil component lifecycles (10/20-year classes).3.5 Stakeholder engagement
• Liaise with the Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS), provincial Water Services Authorities (Ehlanzeni DM, Greater Tzaneen, Makhado, uMkhanyakude DM), and municipal engineers on infrastructure standards, co-maintenance arrangements, and cost-sharing Service Level Agreement negotiations.
• Coordinate with DWS-listed certified solar technical partners and Mvula Borehole Drilling (Pty) Ltd to ensure integrated electromechanical and civil maintenance delivery.
• Represent ForAfrika in technical forums and site meetings with government, communities, and Innovation: Africa counterparts during the transition period.
4. Qualifications and Experience
Essential
• Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering (BEng/BSc Eng) from a recognised institution.
• Registration with the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) as a Candidate Engineer, with Professional Engineer (Pr Eng) or Professional Engineering Technologist (Pr Tech Eng) registration strongly preferred.
• Minimum five (5) years of progressive experience in civil/structural engineering for water supply infrastructure — reservoirs, elevated tanks, pipelines, and rural water schemes.
• Demonstrated working knowledge of SANS standards applicable to water infrastructure (including SANS 241:2015 and structural/civil codes for reinforced-concrete water-retaining structures).
• Proven experience in condition assessment, structural inspection, and rehabilitation of water-retaining structures.
• Experience preparing scopes of work, bills of quantities, and supervising contractors.
• Valid driver's licence and willingness to travel extensively (up to 60%) to remote rural sites across three provinces.Desirable
• MSc/MEng in Civil, Structural, or Water Engineering.
• Experience in the NGO/development sector or donor-funded WASH programmes.
• Familiarity with solar-powered water systems, borehole infrastructure, and rural water utility operations.
• Experience engaging municipal Water Services Authorities and DWS regulatory frameworks (Water Services Act, including Section 19 Water Service Intermediary arrangements).
• Proficiency in AutoCAD/Civil 3D, EPANET or equivalent hydraulic modelling tools, and GIS applications.
• Proficiency in one or more of IsiZulu, Sepedi, or Siswati is an advantage.

about_role:
SAICA has embarked on an exciting transformation to become an insights-driven, technology-enabled, and AIpowered organisation. As part of our journey, we are streamlining processes, enhancing our digital capabilities,and strengthening our focus on sustainability in the accounting profession.
This transformation presents an opportunity for you to grow and contribute to SAICA’s vision in a redefined,future-fit role. We are looking for passionate, skilled professionals who are eager to innovate, embrace datadriven decision-making, and help shape the future of the profession.
Purpose of the job
The Thuthuka and other Schools projects run by SAICA’s Thuthuka Division focus on three strategic objectives:
• To grow the number of CAs(SA), AGAs(SA) and ATs(SA);
• To transform the demographics of the profession to match the country’s demographic profile; and
• To introduce projects which will benefit society at large. The Thuthuka programmes focus on providing support to African and Coloured learners in overcoming barriers to their success through their studies towards becoming CAs (SA). This support begins at high-school level and continues until qualification.
The Schools projects focus on building the CA pipeline.
The objectives of this position are:
• To implement projects in order to promote the CA, AGA, and AT designations and the accountancy profession amongst learners (career exposure platforms).
• To implement projects that promote the importance of mathematics for learners seeking to follow the CA and AGA profession.
• To implement career awareness projects that promote the importance of the involvement of parents and other stakeholders in the education of the learners. Viz:- Educators, principals and district Officials
• To implement projects in order to promote the CA, AGA, and AT designations, the accountancy profession and key competencies such as ethics and financial literacy amongst learners and students.
• To Establish and maintain relationships with related Stakeholders such as the Profession at Large and the Department of Education.
• To implement projects in order to promote the CA, AGA, and AT designations, the accountancy profession and key competencies such as ethics amongst trainees and young professionals.
• To collaborate with other professions who run Maths initiatives.
• SAICA is responsive to all matters relating to transformation inside and outside the profession and timeously addresses these matters as they arise. Influences transformation agendas in other professions.

Regional Marketing Specialist – Africa (English & French Markets)
Main Responsibilities – Regional Activation & Market Execution
The Regional Marketing Specialist Africa is responsible for the regional activation of the company's marketing strategy, ensuring marketing activities contribute to funnel generation, brand visibility, and the roll-out of regional marketing deliverables in line with agreed strategy and budgets.
The successful candidate must have native-level English proficiency.
The Africa office is located in Umhlanga, South Africa. Office presence is required (minimum 2 days per week). Occasional travel across Africa for events, meetings and visits to the Casablanca office in Morocco is also required. The role reports to the Head of Marketing and Communications EMEA.
The Regional Marketing Specialist Africa comprises of 4 main areas:
1. Event Management
End-to-end planning, coordination, and execution of regional events aligned with the company's marketing strategy and commercial priorities.
This includes:
- Trade shows and exhibitions
- Industry seminars and technical events
- Company-hosted customer and industry events
- Distributor and partner events in company offices or at partner sites
- Technical webinars (native or in cooperation with partners)
Responsibilities include management and delivery of the event KPIs, coordination with internal stakeholders and/or partners, brand messaging, and post-event reporting to ensure activities contribute to the region's sales opportunity funnel.
2. Channel Partner Marketing (Co-op Programmes)
Generation, activation, monitoring and analysis of marketing activities executed jointly with channel partners and distributors. These initiatives may include:
- Sponsorships
- Co-exhibiting at events
- Visibility on partner websites or platforms
- Co-branded literature and promotional assets
- Videos and webinars
- Media packs
- Promotional merchandising
- Other co-op marketing initiatives agreed with partners
The role ensures partner activities align with regional strategy and channel needs, acting as a liaison with partners and distributors to support funnel KPIs.
3. Regional Market Activation
Localisation and activation of central marketing campaigns within the region's markets, as well as development and execution of targeted regional initiatives. This includes:
- Activation of global or central marketing campaigns in the region
- Regional campaign activation ("market-making")
- Influencer collaboration and management
- Vertical Media & PR activation
- Regional newsletters, case studies, videos, and market research initiatives designed to increase brand awareness, reach and relevance within the region.
4. Reporting, KPI Management & Regional Coordination
The role delivers on the delivery of regional marketing KPIs by:
- Monitoring marketing activity, performance and ROI
- Providing regular reporting on regional marketing activities and results
- Supporting KPI tracking and recommending corrective actions as required
- Coordinating with central marketing teams and commercial stakeholders to ensure alignment with strategy and budgets
Digital & Social Media Scope
Digital marketing, website management, design, and social media channel management are handled by the central marketing team. Regional Marketing Specialists will provide regional content as relevant. The regional role focuses on field activation, partner engagement, and event execution rather than digital and social media platform management.

Deliver the quality assurance that keeps Africa's most loved Merchant Operating Platform reliable, secure and ready for every release.

Why This Role Matters
Every merchant onboarding journey, customer interaction and Salesforce enhancement depends on quality. As CRM QA & Testing Manager, you will ensure every CRM solution is thoroughly tested, every release is production-ready and every deployment strengthens confidence in our technology.
You will lead CRM quality assurance across the Salesforce ecosystem, establishing testing standards, driving automation and ensuring every release meets the highest standards of reliability, performance and security. From test strategy and defect management to user acceptance testing and governance, you will build a culture where quality is embedded into every stage of delivery.
About Lesaka
Lesaka is a fintech company on a mission to digitise commerce in Africa. We are listed on NASDAQ (LSAK) and the JSE (LSK) and serve merchants, consumers and enterprises across the continent. From spaza shops and taxi ranks to restaurants and city traders, our products power the small exchanges and the big steps of African commerce.
One platform. Many products. One ambition: to be the most loved Merchant Operating Platform in Africa.

Our strategy starts from a simple operating truth. Exceptional customer experiences come from exceptional staff experiences. We balance four pillars across everything we do:
•
Customer Experience
•
Staff Happiness
•
Cost Discipline
•
Risk Control
Each one amplifies the others when properly aligned. We have organised around one merchant journey with clear execution and accountability.
Our North Star
Deliver exceptional experiences to our customers and our staff.
We measure ourselves against CHAP (Customer Happiness), SHAP (Staff Happiness), Cost-to-Serve Efficiency and Regulatory Impact.
Happy customers. Happy staff. Disciplined cost. Controlled risk.

You will lead the CRM Quality Assurance and Testing function, ensuring every Salesforce enhancement, integration and release is validated through structured testing, robust governance and continuous quality improvement.
Working closely with CRM Development, Product, Architecture, Sales and Operations teams, you will define testing strategies, oversee release quality and build automated testing capabilities that improve delivery confidence and reduce production risk.
The role contributes directly to Customer Experience through reliable CRM releases, Cost Discipline through testing automation and quality improvements, and Risk Control through disciplined testing, governance and defect prevention.
You will lead a team of three quality assurance specialists responsible for protecting the quality and stability of the CRM platform.

Develop test plans aligned to project timelines and business priorities.

The Security Manager shall receive, assess, verify, and act on security intelligence aimed at preventing theft and collusion.
5. Security Contractor and Guard Force Management
The Security Manager shall oversee and hold accountable all contracted security providers and on‑site guarding personnel.
6. Gate Security, Searches, and Alcohol Testing
The Security Manager shall ensure strict enforcement of access control, searches, and substance‑testing procedures.
7. Night Shift and After‑Hours Oversight
The Security Manager shall maintain a visible and unpredictable security presence outside normal operating hours.
8. Theft Prevention and Loss Reduction
The Security Manager shall be directly accountable for reducing theft and loss through prevention, detection, deterrence and Security Improvement Projects.
The Security Manager shall continuously identify risks and implement measurable security enhancements.
10. Reporting and Management Communication
The Security Manager shall provide accurate, timely, and actionable reporting to management. Submit a complete monthly security report by the each month.

Senior Credit Risk Analyst - PayJustNow
Purpose of the role:
This role exists to turn fragmented data into profitable lending decisions. The business originates credit across two very different products — a high-volume, thin-margin, short-tenor BNPL book and a longer-dated retail instalment loan book — and the data that should inform those decisions currently sits in silos: bureau feeds in one system, transactional and behavioural data in another, merchant and collections data elsewhere again.
The Senior Credit Risk & Decision Scientist is accountable for three connected outcomes:
• Data optimisation across silos — building a single, governed, decision-ready view of the customer by integrating bureau, internal and alternative data sources, and eliminating duplicated or unused data spend.
• Scorecard build and monitoring — developing, validating, deploying and continuously monitoring application, behavioural, affordability and collections scorecards across both product lines.
• Account origination — designing and optimising the end-to-end origination decision engine: policy rules, cut-offs, limit assignment, affordability assessment, fraud screening and champion/challenger strategy.Success is measured commercially. The role is expected to demonstrably improve risk-adjusted return — higher approval rates at constant or lower loss, lower cost of data acquisition, and faster decisioning — not simply to produce models.
Key Responsibilities:
Data Optimization across business silo's:
• Map the full credit data estate across origination, servicing, collections, merchant/partner and marketing systems; document lineage, ownership, refresh cadence, quality and cost of every source.
• Design and own a consolidated credit data mart / feature store that serves modelling, decisioning and reporting from a single set of definitions, removing conflicting versions of the same metric.
• Integrate and rationalise the three data families the business depends on:
• Bureau data — scores, enquiry data, tradeline and payment-profile history, adverse and judgment data, affordability indicators.
• Internal data — application, transactional, repayment and arrears behaviour, customer tenure, cross-product holdings, merchant and basket-level data, servicing and contact history.
• Alternative data — bank transaction / open-banking data, device and digital footprint, telco and payment-behaviour signals, geospatial and psychometric indicators where lawful and predictive.
• Run a continuous cost-to-value assessment of every paid external data source: quantify incremental lift per Rand of bureau or alternative-data spend and retire, renegotiate or re-sequence calls that do not pay for themselves.
• Implement tiered / cascaded data-call strategies so expensive attributes are only purchased where they change the decision.
• Define and enforce data quality standards, reconciliation controls and monitoring for all decision-critical feeds; own the resolution path when a feed degrades or a bureau attribute drifts.
• Partner with Data Engineering to productionise pipelines, and with Product and Finance so that a single agreed set of risk and profitability metrics is used across the business.Scorecard Development:
• Own the full model lifecycle for application, behavioural, affordability, fraud-propensity and collections scorecards across BNPL and retail loan portfolios.
• Construct reliable modelling samples: target definition, performance and outcome windows, exclusions, reject inference, and correction for the short performance windows and rapid repeat-usage cycles typical of BNPL.
• Engineer and select features from bureau, internal and alternative sources; apply appropriate binning, WoE/IV analysis, segmentation and multicollinearity treatment.
• Build models using the right tool for the job — logistic regression and scorecard scaling where explainability and regulatory defensibility are required; gradient boosting and other machine-learning techniques where lift justifies them, supported by explainability output (SHAP or equivalent).
• Validate rigorously: out-of-time and out-of-sample testing, Gini/KS/AUC, calibration, stability, segment-level performance and fairness/disparate-impact testing.
• Produce model documentation to internal model-risk and audit standard, and present models to the Credit or Model Risk Committee for approval if needed.
• Support deployment into the decision engine and sign off implementation testing — confirming that the scored production population matches the development specification, attribute for attribute.Scorecard monitoring and model governance:
• Own the full model lifecycle for application, behavioural, affordability, fraud-propensity and collections scorecards across BNPL and retail loan portfolios.
• Construct reliable modelling samples: target definition, performance and outcome windows, exclusions, reject inference, and correction for the short performance windows and rapid repeat-usage cycles typical of BNPL.
• Engineer and select features from bureau, internal and alternative sources; apply appropriate binning, WoE/IV analysis, segmentation and multicollinearity treatment.
• Build models using the right tool for the job — logistic regression and scorecard scaling where explainability and regulatory defensibility are required; gradient boosting and other machine-learning techniques where lift justifies them, supported by explainability output (SHAP or equivalent).
• Validate rigorously: out-of-time and out-of-sample testing, Gini/KS/AUC, calibration, stability, segment-level performance and fairness/disparate-impact testing.
• Produce model documentation to internal model-risk and audit standard, and present models to the Credit or Model Risk Committee for approval if needed.
• Support deployment into the decision engine and sign off implementation testing — confirming that the scored production population matches the development specification, attribute for attribute.Account Origination and Decision Strategy:
• Own the origination decision logic end-to-end: pre-screen, identity and fraud checks, bureau and alternative data calls, scorecard execution, affordability assessment, policy rules, cut-off setting, limit assignment and referral treatment.
• Optimise approval-rate versus loss trade-offs using swap-set analysis; quantify the profit impact of every proposed cut-off or policy change before it goes live.
• Design initial credit limit and limit-increase strategies for BNPL, balancing basket-size conversion and merchant experience against exposure at risk.
• Build and run a disciplined champion/challenger and A/B testing programme, including test design, sample sizing, holdout maintenance and readout, so that strategy changes are evidence-based rather than opinion-based.
• Reduce friction and decision latency: increase straight-through-processing rates, cut manual referrals, and shorten time-to-decision without increasing loss.
• Work with Fraud to separate first-party and third-party fraud losses from credit losses, and ensure origination strategy treats them differently.
• Feed origination insight back into Product, Merchant and Marketing teams — which channels, merchants, baskets and segments originate profitable accounts, and which do not.Commercial and Profitability impact:
• Translate analytics into commercial recommendations with quantified rand-value impact, and defend them to Credit, Finance and Exco.
• Contribute to credit loss forecasting and to the annual budget and business planning cycle.Other:
• Act as the analytical authority in Credit Committee forums; present clearly to non-technical audiences.
• Mentor junior analysts, review their code and models, and raise the analytical standard of the team.

about_role:
Introduction to the VKB Group
The VKB Group is an agricultural company, providing support to farmers and producing straight-from-the farm-foods for consumers. Apart from the various consumer brands, the VKB Group is also represented by its regional brands: VKB, GWK and NTK. Our roots are firmly planted in agriculture with farming at our core, continuously growing and evolving throughout the years.
Starting with providing everything needed on the farm to produce food, we now also operate in all areas of the food supply chain: processing, logistics, and national and global market channels.
This “house of brands” we’ve established with the support of our farmer shareholders is the foundation for building the agribusiness of the future.
Grow Your Career Where Agriculture Meets Innovation
At the VKB Group, we are passionate about agriculture and the people who make it possible. As one of South Africa's leading agribusinesses, we support farmers across the entire value chain, from production inputs to processing, logistics, and market access.
Our success is built on our people and our values. We are humble enough to learn, hungry to grow, smart in our decisions, bold in our actions, and stronger together as team players. If you are passionate about agriculture, enjoy working with people, and want to build a rewarding sales career in agricultural mechanization, we would like to hear from you.
About the Opportunity
We are looking for a motivated and energetic Junior Whole Goods Marketer to join our Mechanization team in Bethlehem.
This role offers an exciting opportunity to work with world-class CASE IH agricultural equipment while developing your skills in sales, customer relationships, precision farming technologies, and agricultural machinery.
You will work closely with farmers and agricultural producers, helping them identify the right mechanization solutions to improve productivity and profitability.
Whether you are already working in agricultural equipment sales or have a strong agricultural background with an interest in machinery and sales, this could be the next step in your career.

Sales & Customer Relationships
• Market and sell CASE IH tractors, combines, and other agricultural equipment.
• Build and maintain strong relationships with farmers and agricultural businesses.

• Coordinate equipment logistics and delivery processes.
• Adhere to company policies, safety standards, and risk management practices.What We Are Looking For

• Knowledge of agricultural mechanization and precision farming practices.

• Experience working directly with commercial farmers.The Ideal Candidate
You are:
• Passionate about agriculture and customer service.
• Comfortable engaging with farmers and building long-term relationships.
• Commercially minded and motivated by achieving results.
• Technically curious and eager to learn about agricultural equipment.

ROLE PURPOSE

1. Programme Background
ForAfrika is a leading African humanitarian and development organisation operating in eight countries, with a vision of an Africa that thrives. Under a three-year grant, ForAfrika South Africa will assume full operational responsibility for 101 solar-powered rural water supply systems across Mpumalanga, Limpopo and KwaZulu-Natal.
The programme operates through a three-layer architecture: Layer 1 (Core Operations and Maintenance), Layer 2 (Food Security and Livelihoods to Social Enterprise), and Layer 3 (Hub Economic Activation), converting each water site into a community-owned Solar Water Enterprise Hub. ForAfrika's role is to maintain, operate, and transfer these systems to community ownership, ensuring compliance with the South African National Standards for water quality throughout.
2. Purpose of the Position
The Civil Engineer provides oversight of civil infrastructure across the South Africa portfolio. The position is responsible for the structural integrity, inspection, maintenance planning, and standards compliance of all civil works.
The role is central to determining the technical condition assessment of all sites, the site-tier triage, the remediation and drawdown planning of the Replacement Capex Reserve for civil components.
3. Key Responsibilities
3.1 Technical condition assessment and site-tier triage
• Lead the civil and structural component of the site-by-site technical condition assessment across all the sites within the first three months of the programme, covering tanks, towers, distribution networks, valves and fittings, pump houses, and civil structures.
• Contribute civil condition data to the site-tier triage and identify civil components requiring Day 1 or Year 1 replacement funded from the Replacement Capex Reserve.
• Support full condition assessment and Tier C remediation at the named priority sites.
• Verify and reconcile the civil elements of the sites including as-built and structural drawings (3m, 7m, and 10m tank towers; the 30-kilolitre high-capacity tank class), borehole completion reports, and site asset registers.3.2 Routine civil inspection and maintenance oversight
• Design and implement the routine structural inspection cycle for civil infrastructure across the portfolio, integrated into the Tier 2 quarterly inspection programme.
• Procure, scope, and supervise specialist-chartered engineering inspections of 30-kilolitre reinforced-concrete tanks in compliance with applicable SANS standards, managing the specialist sub-contract and certifying deliverables.
• Develop civil maintenance specifications, bills of quantities, and scopes of work for repairs, rehabilitation, and upgrades; supervise contractors and certify completed works.
• Assess and prioritise Parent-site civil infrastructure within the cluster maintenance model, recognising that a Parent borehole failure cascades to hydraulically dependent Child sites.
• Support reactive repair response for civil failures in line with the tiered service-impact protocol.3.3 Standards compliance, quality assurance and reporting
• Ensure all civil works, inspections, and rehabilitation comply with applicable SANS standards and relevant national and municipal regulations, and that water infrastructure supports compliance with SANS 241:2015 water quality requirements.
• Maintain the civil asset register, structural inspection records, drawings library, and defect logs within the programme's field management system.
• Contribute civil infrastructure data and analysis to monthly cluster reports, quarterly donor reports to Donor, and the MEAL dashboard .
• Support the DMEAL team with means-of-verification documentation for infrastructure-related KPIs.3.4 Capacity building and transition
• Train ForAfrika field engineers, community pump attendants, and Water Management Committee members in basic civil infrastructure surveillance (visual inspection of tanks, towers, standpipes, and soakaways) as part of the Tier 1 community operator curriculum.
• Contribute civil O&M content to site-level O&M manuals, sustainability plans, and handover documentation supporting the Year 3 transition to community and Water Services Authority management.
• Advise on civil aspects of Capital Sinking Fund calibration, aligning contribution rates to civil component lifecycles (10/20-year classes).3.5 Stakeholder engagement
• Liaise with the Department of Water and Sanitation (DWS), provincial Water Services Authorities (Ehlanzeni DM, Greater Tzaneen, Makhado, uMkhanyakude DM), and municipal engineers on infrastructure standards, co-maintenance arrangements, and cost-sharing Service Level Agreement negotiations.
• Coordinate with DWS-listed certified solar technical partners and Mvula Borehole Drilling (Pty) Ltd to ensure integrated electromechanical and civil maintenance delivery.
• Represent ForAfrika in technical forums and site meetings with government, communities.
4. Qualifications and Experience
Essential
• Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering (BEng/BSc Eng) from a recognised institution.
• Registration with the Engineering Council of South Africa (ECSA) as a Candidate Engineer, with Professional Engineer (Pr Eng) or Professional Engineering Technologist (Pr Tech Eng) registration strongly preferred.
• Minimum five (5) years of progressive experience in civil/structural engineering for water supply infrastructure — reservoirs, elevated tanks, pipelines, and rural water schemes.
• Demonstrated working knowledge of SANS standards applicable to water infrastructure (including SANS 241:2015 and structural/civil codes for reinforced-concrete water-retaining structures).
• Proven experience in condition assessment, structural inspection, and rehabilitation of water-retaining structures.
• Experience preparing scopes of work, bills of quantities, and supervising contractors.
• Valid driver's licence and willingness to travel extensively (up to 60%) to remote rural sites across three provinces.Desirable
• MSc/MEng in Civil, Structural, or Water Engineering.
• Experience in the NGO/development sector or donor-funded WASH programmes.
• Familiarity with solar-powered water systems, borehole infrastructure, and rural water utility operations.
• Experience engaging municipal Water Services Authorities and DWS regulatory frameworks (Water Services Act, including Section 19 Water Service Intermediary arrangements).

The ideal candidate is someone who understands apparel and footwear retail, enjoys working with stock and data, and can turn information into practical action.
This person must not only be able to pull reports, but must also understand what the numbers mean, why stock issues happen, and how to solve them. They must understand the mechanics of inventory planning from the ground up and be able to follow through from planning, to communication, to execution.
The right candidate will be structured, analytical, practical, and hands-on, with a strong ability to solve problems and improve how stock flows through the business.
Job Purpose
The Apparel Inventory Planner is responsible for ensuring that the right products are available in the right stores, in the right quantities, at the right time.
This role manages stock planning, replenishment, allocations, size curves, transfers, stock balancing, and inventory reporting across retail stores, online channels, and warehouse locations.
The role requires someone who understands inventory planning from the ground up — not only the reporting side, but also the working mechanics behind stock movement, replenishment, allocations, store demand, ERP accuracy, warehouse flow, and execution across the business.
The Apparel Inventory Planner plays a critical role in improving stock availability, reducing stock-outs, managing slow-moving stock, supporting better buying decisions, and ensuring that inventory supports sales, customer demand, and profitability.
Key Responsibilities
1. Stock Planning & Replenishment
●    Plan and manage stock levels across all stores, online channels, and warehouse locations.
●    Monitor weekly sales, stock-on-hand, sell-through, weeks-of-cover, and stock availability.
●    Identify fast-moving, slow-moving, and out-of-stock products.
●    Recommend replenishment actions based on sales trends, stock holding, store performance, and customer demand.
●    Ensure key styles, best sellers, and core products are available in the correct quantities and sizes.
●    Maintain proper size curves across footwear, apparel, and accessories.
●    Identify gaps in stock availability before they become sales problems.
●    Support the business in maintaining the correct balance between stock availability and stock efficiency.
2. Allocations & Store Stock Balancing
●    Allocate new stock to stores based on sales history, store grading, product type, size demand, store capacity, and available stock.
●    Review stock distribution regularly and recommend store-to-store transfers where required.
●    Ensure stores are not overstocked or understocked in specific products, categories, or sizes.
●    Support new store openings, promotional launches, campaigns, and seasonal product drops with correct stock allocations.
●    Ensure stock is placed where it has the highest chance of selling.
●    Monitor store stock levels and recommend corrective actions where stores are carrying poor size curves, excess stock, or insufficient depth.
3. Inventory Reporting & Analysis
●    Prepare weekly and monthly inventory reports to support decision-making.
●    Report on key inventory metrics, including:
○    Stock-on-hand
○    Sell-through
○    Weeks-of-cover
○    Stock-outs
○    Slow movers
○    Best sellers
○    Store performance by category
○    Size availability
○    Transfer requirements
○    Replenishment needs
●    Analyse product, store, category, and size performance.
●    Identify risks and opportunities in the stock position.
●    Translate sales and stock data into clear, practical actions.
●    Provide management with meaningful insights, not just reports.
4. ERP & System Management
●    Maintain and monitor accurate product, stock, and planning information on the ERP system.
●    Ensure ERP data supports accurate planning, replenishment, reporting, and stock decision-making.
●    Monitor transfers, shipments, receipts, and stock movements to ensure they are processed correctly.
●    Follow up on unconfirmed shipments, outstanding transfers, receiving issues, and system discrepancies.
●    Work closely with the Stock Controller to identify and resolve stock accuracy issues.
●    Assist with stock take preparation, variance analysis, and stock accuracy improvement.
●    Understand how system transactions impact physical stock, store availability, and reporting accuracy.
5. Planning Principles & Execution
●    Understand planning principles from the ground up through to execution.
●    Understand the full working mechanics of inventory planning, including how sales, stock, replenishment, allocations, transfers, buying, warehouse movement, and store performance all connect.
●    Build planning recommendations that are practical, executable, and aligned with business reality.
●    Identify the root cause of stock issues rather than only reacting to symptoms.
●    Ensure that planning decisions are followed through into action.
●    Work across teams to make sure that plans are implemented properly and that stock movements are completed.
6. Buying & Product Support
●    Support the buying team with stock history, sales data, product performance, and size curve insights.
●    Provide recommendations on reorder quantities, product depth, store allocations, and replenishment requirements.
●    Assist in identifying products that should be repeated, discontinued, marked down, transferred, or rebalanced.
●    Support seasonal, capsule, promotional, and core product planning.
●    Provide input into future stock buys based on actual store and product performance.
●    Help ensure that buying decisions are informed by data, store demand, and practical stock flow.
7. Store & Warehouse Communication
●    Communicate stock movements, transfer requirements, replenishment priorities, and stock actions clearly to stores and warehouse teams.
●    Follow up with stores on receiving, transfers, stock discrepancies, and stock availability issues.
●    Work with store teams to understand customer demand, stock gaps, size requests, and product feedback.
●    Ensure stores follow the correct processes for stock movement, receiving, transfers, and reporting.
●    Work with warehouse teams to ensure stock is dispatched, received, and processed accurately and timeously.
●    Escalate stock issues where needed and drive practical solutions.

Maintenance Manager
A permanent opportunity to lead, plan, and control all maintenance activities across production equipment and site facilities to ensure maximum plant availability, operational reliability, and safety. The role is based in the Ottery or Philippi branch within the packaging sector.
About Our Client
The company operates within the manufacturing and packaging sector, focusing on production equipment, site facilities, and utilities. The organization utilizes advanced engineering systems, automation, and structured maintenance frameworks to drive sustainability and environmental impact awareness.
The Role: Maintenance Manager
The Maintenance Manager exists to lead, plan, and control all maintenance activities across production equipment and site facilities. The role contributes to the business by ensuring maximum plant availability, operational reliability, and safety at an optimal total cost while driving preventive and predictive maintenance strategies. The main focus areas involve governing legal compliance as the legally appointed GMR 2.1 competent person, leading a multi-disciplinary technical team, and directly supervising the safe use, operation, and maintenance of all machinery on site.
Key Responsibilities
• Manage 7–10 years of industrial maintenance experience, including 3–5 years in a leadership or supervisory role within a manufacturing environment.
• Act as the designated, legally appointed GMR 2.1 competent person supervising site machinery to ensure total compliance with the OHS Act and General Machinery Regulations.
• Own and execute the maintenance master plan across preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance frameworks using a Computerized Maintenance Management System.
• Implement Reliability-Centred Maintenance, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, and root cause analysis methodologies to resolve operational losses.
• Deploy and govern the Computerized Maintenance Management System, including the asset register, Bills of Materials, PM routines, work order management, backlog control, and equipment history.
• Support high equipment availability and Overall Equipment Effectiveness through disciplined PM compliance, breakdown responses, and effective technical escalation.
• Lead, coach, and develop the technical maintenance team consisting of Maintenance Supervisors, Artisans, and Technicians while managing the annual maintenance OPEX and CAPEX budgets.
• Apply company quality principles, adhere to Good Manufacturing Practices, and strictly comply with site-specific Food Safety Management Systems and FSSC standards.

Introduction to the VKB Group
The VKB Group is an agricultural company, providing support to farmers and producing straight-from-the farm-foods for consumers. Apart from the various consumer brands, the VKB Group is also represented by its regional brands: VKB, GWK and NTK. Our roots are firmly planted in agriculture with farming at our core, continuously growing and evolving throughout the years.
Starting with providing everything needed on the farm to produce food, we now also operate in all areas of the food supply chain: processing, logistics, and national and global market channels.
This “house of brands” we’ve established with the support of our farmer shareholders is the foundation for building the agribusiness of the future.
